- Root: و-ق-ى (wa-qā-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Protection, guarding, shielding from harm; the root denotes warding off that which is feared.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqwā (God-consciousness) is the soul's protective shield against divine displeasure — placing a barrier between oneself and the object of fear.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical preservation; metaphorical sense is the heart's vigilant abstention from transgression.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Construction (الشّرط) — The imperative "اتق" followed by "حيثما" establishes a general conditional clause governing all spatial and temporal contexts.
chapters.translation:
The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Fear God wherever you are, and follow up a misdeed with a good deed that will erase it, and treat people with excellent character." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith," and in some of his authoritative copies: "A good and sound (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.")

The twenty-third (hadith): From Muʿādh, may God Most High be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, inform me of a deed that will admit me into Paradise and distance me from the Fire." He said: "You have asked about something momentous, yet it is easy for whomsoever God Most High makes it easy: that you worship God and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, give the alms (zakāh), fast Ramaḍān, and make pilgrimage to the House." Then he said: "Shall I not guide you to the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire, and a man's prayer in the depths of the night." Then he recited: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} — "Their sides forsake their beds" — until he reached {«يَعْمَلُونَ»} — "what they used to do." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and the peak of its hump? It is jihad." Then he said: "Shall I not inform you of the linchpin of all of that?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." So he took hold of his tongue and said: "Restrain this upon yourself." I said: "O Prophet of God, will we indeed be held accountable for what we speak?" He said: "May your mother lose you! Is anything that topples people into the Fire on their faces — or on their nostrils — other than the harvest of their tongues?" (Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good and sound hadith." "Dhurwat al-sanām" means its summit, pronounced with ḍammah or kasrah on the dhāl.)

The twenty-fourth (hadith): From al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, admonished us with an admonition at which hearts trembled and eyes shed tears. We said: "O Messenger of God, this seems like the admonition of one bidding farewell, so counsel us." He said: "I counsel you to fear God, and to hear and obey — even if a slave is appointed over you. For whoever among you lives will see much disagreement. So adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided, divinely-directed caliphs after me; bite onto it with your molar teeth. And beware of newly-invented matters, for every innovation (bidʿah) is a misguidance." (Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good and sound hadith.")

The twenty-fifth (hadith): From Ibn ʿAbbās, may God Most High be pleased with them both, who said: I was behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day, and he said: "O young lad, I shall teach you words: Preserve God and He will preserve you. Preserve God and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask of God; and when you seek help, seek help from God. And know that if the entire community gathered together to benefit you with something, they could not benefit you except with something God has already written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you with something, they could not harm you except with something God has already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the scrolls have dried." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good and sound hadith." And in a narration other than al-Tirmidhī's: "Preserve God and you will find Him before you. Acknowledge God in times of ease, and He will acknowledge you in times of hardship. And know that what missed you was never to befall you, and what befell you was never to miss you." And at its end: "And know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease.")

The twenty-sixth (hadith): The hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, from his father ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God Most High be pleased with them both, concerning faith in divine decree (al-qadar), the elucidation of faith (īmān), Islam, excellence (iḥsān), and the signs of the Hour. These are the hadiths mentioned by Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may God Most High have mercy on him. And among what carries their meaning is one, namely:

The twenty-seventh (hadith): From Sufyān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, may God Most High be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, tell me about Islam a statement after which I need not ask anyone other than you." He said: "Say: I believe in God, then remain steadfast." (Narrated by Muslim.)

The twenty-eighth (hadith): From Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "If you feel no shame, then do as you wish." (Narrated by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ.)

The twenty-ninth (hadith): From Jābir, may God Most High be pleased with him, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "Have you considered: if I pray the five prescribed prayers, fast Ramaḍān, treat the lawful as lawful and the unlawful as unlawful, and add nothing more to that — will I enter Paradise?" He said: "Yes." (Narrated by Muslim.)

CHAPTER: On the Reality of Sincerity (al-Ikhlāṣ) and Truthfulness (al-Ṣidq)

As for sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ), God Most High said: {«وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ»} — "And they were not commanded except to worship God, devoting religion exclusively to Him" — the verse. And we have narrated from Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, may God Most High be pleased with him, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, "What is sincerity?" He said: "I asked Gabriel what sincerity is, and he said: 'I asked the Lord of Might what sincerity is, and He said: It is a secret from My secrets which I have deposited in the heart of whomever I love among My servants.'"

And we have narrated from the master Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, may God Most High have mercy on him, who said: "Sincerity is the singling out of the Truth in obedience by intention — that one intends by his obedience to draw near to God Most High, and nothing else: not self-display before a creature, nor acquisition of praise among people, nor seeking commendation from creation, nor any other meaning besides drawing near to God Most High." He said: "And it may validly be said that sincerity is the guarding against observing persons."

And we have narrated from the master Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq, may God Most High have mercy on him, who said: "Sincerity is the guarding against observing creation, and truthfulness is the guarding against scrutinizing the self. So the sincere one has no ostentation (riyāʾ), and the truthful one has no self-admiration (iʿjāb)."

And we have narrated from Abū Yaʿqūb al-Sūsī, may God Most High be pleased with him, who said: "When they witness sincerity within their sincerity, their sincerity stands in need of further sincerity."

And we have narrated from the noble master Dhū al-Nūn, may God Most High be pleased with him, who said: "Three are among the signs of sincerity: the equal standing of praise and blame from the common people, the forgetting of seeing one's deeds within one's deeds, and seeking the reward of the deed only in the Hereafter."

And from Abū ʿUthmān al-Maghribī, may God Most High have mercy on him, who said: "Sincerity is the forgetting of observing creation through the constancy of gazing upon the Creator."

And from Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī, may God Most High have mercy on him, who said: "Sincerity is that the servant's deeds be equal in the outward and the inward."

And from the noble master Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, may God Most High have mercy on him, who said: "Abandoning deeds..."

chapters.title_en: Section 6 — On Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) and Truthfulness (Ṣidq)
chapters.arabic_text: لاجل الناس رياء والعمل لاجل الناس شرك والاخلاص أن يعافيك الله منهما. وعن السيد الجليل أبي محمد سهل بن عبد الله التستري رحمه الله تعالى أنه سئل أي شيء أشد على النفس قال إخلاص لأنه شيء ليس لها فيه نصيب. وعن يوسف بن الحسين رحمه الله تعالى قال أعز شيء في الدنيا الاخلاص. وعن أبي عثمان المغربي رحمه الله تعالى قال اخلاص العوام ما لا يكون للنفس فيه حظ وإخلاص الخواص ما يجري عليهم لا بهم فتبدو منهم الطاعات وهم عنها بمعزل ولا تقع لهم عليها رؤية ولا لهم عليها اعتداد. وروينا عن السيد الجليل الإمام التابعي مكحول رضي الله تعالى عنه قال ما أخلص عبد قط أربعين يوما إلا ظهرت ينابيع الحكمة من قلبه على لسانه. وروينا عن سهل التستري قال من زهد في الدنيا أربعين يوما صادقا من قلبه مخلصا في ذلك ظهرت له الكرامات ومن لم يظهر له فإنه عدم الصدق في زهده فقيل لسهل كيف تظهر له الكرامات قال يأخذ ما يشاء كما # # يشاء من حيث يشاء. قال سهل التستري رحمه الله نظر الأكياس في تفسير الاخلاص فلم يجدوا غير هذا أن تكون حركته وسكونه في سره وعلانيته لله تعالى وحده لا يمازجه شيء لا نفس ولا هوى ولا دنيا. وقال السري رحمه الله لا تعمل للناس شيئا ولا تترك لهم شيئا ولا تعط لهم شيئا ولا تكشف لهم شيئا. وأما الصدق فقال الله تعالى (يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين) وروينا عن الأستاذ القشيري رحمه الله قال الصدق عماد الأمر وبه تمامه وفيه نظامه قال وأقل الصدق استواء السر والعلانية. وروينا عن سهل رحمه الله تعالى قال لا يشم رائحة الصدق عبد داهن نفسه أو غيره. وروينا عن ذي النون قال الصدق سيف الله ما وضع على شيء إلا قطعه. وروينا عن السيد الجليل الإمام العارف الحارث المحاسبي رحمه الله تعالى قال الصادق هو الذي لا يبالي لو خرج كل قدر له في قلوب الخلق من أجل صلاح قلبه ولا يحب إطلاع الناس على مثاقيل من حسن عمله ولا يكره أن يطلع الناس على السيئ من عمله فإن كراهته دليل على أنه يحب الزيادة عندهم وليس هذا من إخلاص الصديقين. وقيل إذا طلبت من الله تعالى الصدق أعطاك مرآة تبصر فيها ك شيء من عجائب الدنيا والآخرة. وروينا عن السيد الجليل أبي القاسم الجنيد رضي الله تعالى عنه قال الصادق يتقلب في اليوم أربعين مرة والمرائي يثبت على حالة واحدة أربعين سنة قلت معناه أن الصادق يدور مع الحق كيف كان فإذا رأى الفضل الشرعي في أمر عمل به وإن خالف ما كان # واحدةدة بحيث لو عرض له مهم يرجحه الشرع عليه في بعض الأحوال لم يأت بهذا المهم بل يحافظ على حالته لأنه يرائي بعبادته وحاله المخلوقين فيخاف من التغير ذهاب محبتهم إياه فيحافظ على بقائها والصادق يريد بعبادته وجه الله تعالى فحيث رجح الشرع حالا صار إليه ولا يعرج على المخلوقين. وقد بسطت القول في هذه الحكاية في أول شرح المهذب وذكرت دلائلها وأوضحتها بالأمثلة ومقصودها ما ذكرته هنا فاقتصرت عليه والله أعلم. بحيث لو عرض له مهم يرجحه الشرع عليه في بعض الأحوال لم يأت بهذا المهم بل يحافظ على حالته لأنه يرائي بعبادته وحاله المخلوقين فيخاف من التغير ذهاب محبتهم إياه فيحافظ على بقائها والصادق يريد بعبادته وجه الله تعالى فحيث رجح الشرع حالا صار إليه ولا يعرج على المخلوقين. وقد بسطت القول في هذه الحكاية في أول شرح المهذب وذكرت دلائلها وأوضحتها بالأمثلة ومقصودها ما ذكرته هنا فاقتصرت عليه والله أعلم. | | فصل # # اعلم أنه ينبغي لمن أراد شيئا من الطاعات وإن قل أن يحضر النية وهو أن يقصد بعمله رضا الله عز وجل وتكون نيته حال العمل ويدخل في هذا جميع العبادات من الصلاة والصوم والوضوء والتيمم والاعتكاف والحج والزكاة والصدقة وقضاء الحوائج وعيادة المريض واتباع الجنائز وابتداء السلام ورده وتشميت العاطس وإنكار المنكر والأمر بالمعروف وإجابة الدعوة وحضور مجالس العلم والأذكار وزيارة الأخيار والنفقة على الأهل والضيف وإكرام أهل الودوذوي الأرحام ومذاكرة العلم والمناظرة فيه وتكراره وتدريسه وتعليمه ومطالعته وكتابته وتصنيفه والفتاوي وكذلك ما أشبه هذه الأعمال حتى لا ينبغي له إذا أكل أو شرب أو نام يقصد بذلك التقوى على طاعة الله أو راحة البدن للتنشيط للطاعة وكذلك إذا أراد جماع زوجته يقصد إيصالها حقها وتحصيل ولد صالح يعبد الله تعالى واعفاف نفسه وصيانتها من التطلع إلى حرام والفكر فيه فمن حرم النية في هذه الأعمال فقد حرم خيرا عظيما كثيرا ومن وفق لها فقد أعطى فضلا جسيما فنسأل الله الكريم التوفيق لذلك وسائر وجوه الخير ودلائل هذه القاعدة ما قدمناه من قوله رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم) إنما الأعمال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is purity and clarity; khāliṣ is that which is unmixed, free from adulteration—like pure honey or clear water.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, ikhlāṣ is the purification of the act from any motive other than seeking God alone; it is the essence of tawḥīd in action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it denotes extraction and separation (of dross from gold); metaphorically, it is the heart's extraction of the divine will from all competing intentions.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate emphasis (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — used to establish definitions and axiomatic truths, as in "al-ikhlāṣ an yuʿāfiyaka Allāh" (sincerity is that God preserves you...).
chapters.translation:
I say: Acting for the sake of people is ostentation (riyāʾ), and acting for the sake of people is polytheism (shirk). Sincerity (ikhlāṣ) is that God preserves you from both of these.

And it is related from the noble master, Abū Muḥammad Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he was asked: "What thing is most severe upon the soul?" He said: "Sincerity, because it is a thing in which the soul has no share."

And it is related from Yūsuf ibn al-Ḥusayn (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he said: "The most precious thing in this world is sincerity."

And it is related from Abū ʿUthmān al-Maghribī (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he said: "The sincerity of the common people (al-ʿawāmm) is that in which the soul has no portion. The sincerity of the elite (al-khawāṣṣ) is that which flows upon them but not through them—so that acts of obedience appear from them while they are detached from those acts, having neither vision of them nor reckoning of them for themselves."

And we have related from the noble master, the Imām among the Followers (tābiʿī), Makḥūl (may God Most High be pleased with him) that he said: "No servant has ever been sincere for forty days except that springs of wisdom burst forth from his heart upon his tongue."

And we have related from Sahl al-Tustarī that he said: "Whoever abstains from this world (zuhd) for forty days, truthfully from his heart, being sincere in that, miracles (karāmāt) appear to him. And whoever does not have them appear—then he has lacked truthfulness in his abstinence." So it was said to Sahl: "How do miracles appear to him?" He said: "He takes whatever he wishes, however he wishes, from wherever he wishes."

Sahl al-Tustarī (may God Most High have mercy on him) said: "The intelligent ones (al-akyās) examined the interpretation of sincerity and found nothing other than this: that one's movement and stillness, in his secret and in his open, be for God Most High alone—nothing mixing with it: neither soul, nor desire, nor world."

And al-Sarī (may God Most High have mercy on him) said: "Do not do anything for people, do not abandon anything for them, do not give anything to them, and do not reveal anything to them."

As for truthfulness (ṣidq), God Most High said: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ»} ("O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful ones").

And we have related from the master al-Qushayrī (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he said: "Truthfulness is the pillar of the affair; by it is its completion, and in it is its order." He said: "And the least of truthfulness is the equality of the secret and the open."

And we have related from Sahl (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he said: "No servant who flatters himself or others will ever smell the fragrance of truthfulness."

And we have related from Dhū al-Nūn that he said: "Truthfulness is the sword of God—it is not placed upon anything except that it cuts it."

And we have related from the noble master, the Imām, the gnostic (ʿārif), al-Ḥārith al-Muḥāsibī (may God Most High have mercy on him) that he said: "The truthful one is he who does not care if all his standing in the hearts of creation were to depart, for the sake of the soundness of his own heart. He does not love that people should see the weight of an atom of his good deeds, and he does not dislike that people should see the evil of his deeds. For his dislike of that is evidence that he loves increase in their estimation—and this is not from the sincerity of the veracious ones (ṣiddīqīn)."

And it was said: "If you seek truthfulness from God Most High, He gives you a mirror in which you see every wonder of this world and the Hereafter."

And we have related from the noble master, Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd (may God Most High be pleased with him) that he said: "The truthful one turns about forty times in a single day, while the ostentatious one (murāʾī) remains fixed upon a single state for forty years."

I say: Its meaning is that the truthful one revolves with the truth (al-ḥaqq) however it may be. When he sees the legal merit (al-faḍl al-sharʿī) in a matter, he acts upon it even if it contradicts his custom. And when something more important presents itself to him in the Sacred Law, and it is not possible to combine the two, he moves to the more excellent—and he continues thus. Perhaps in a single day he may be upon a hundred states, or a thousand or more, according to his capacity in the gnoses (maʿārif) and the appearance of subtle realities and graces to him.

As for the ostentatious one, he clings to a single state—such that if an important matter presented itself to him which the Sacred Law would deem more preponderant in some circumstances, he does not undertake that important matter, but rather preserves his state. This is because he displays ostentation through his worship and his state to the creatures, and he fears that change would cause the loss of their love for him—so he preserves its continuance.

The truthful one, however, seeks by his worship only the Face of God Most High. So wherever the Sacred Law deems a state more preponderant, he moves to it and does not turn aside to the creatures.

I have already expanded the discussion of this narrative at the beginning of my commentary Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab, and I mentioned its evidences and clarified them with examples. Its intended meaning is what I have mentioned here, so I have confined myself to that. And God knows best.

---

SECTION (Faṣl):

Know that it is incumbent upon whoever desires any act of obedience—however small—to present the intention (niyya), which is that he intend by his action the pleasure of God, Mighty and Majestic. And his intention should be present at the moment of the act. Included in this are all acts of worship: prayer, fasting, ablution (wuḍūʾ), dry ablution (tayammum), seclusion in the mosque (iʿtikāf), pilgrimage (ḥajj), alms (zakāt), charity, fulfilling people's needs, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, initiating the greeting of peace and returning it, responding to the sneezer (tashmīt al-ʿāṭis), forbidding wrong (inkār al-munkar), commanding right (al-amr bi al-maʿrūf), answering invitations, attending gatherings of knowledge and remembrance (dhikr), visiting the righteous, spending upon one's family and guest, honoring those of friendship and kinship, discussing knowledge, debating in it, repeating it, teaching it, instructing it, studying it, writing it, authoring it, and issuing legal rulings (fatāwā)—and likewise whatever resembles these acts.

Indeed, it is fitting that when he eats, drinks, or sleeps, he intend thereby to gain strength for obedience to God, or the rest of the body for vigor in obedience. Likewise, when he desires intercourse with his wife, he should intend thereby to give her her right, to obtain a righteous child who worships God Most High, and to protect himself and keep himself chaste from looking toward the forbidden and from thinking about it.

Whoever is deprived of intention in these acts has been deprived of a great and abundant good. And whoever is granted success in it has been given a tremendous favor. So we ask God, the Generous, for success in that and in all aspects of goodness.

The evidence for this principle is what we have already presented from the saying of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): {«إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ»} ("Indeed, actions are but by intentions...").

chapters.title_en: Section 7 — On Intentions (al-Niyyāt) and Their Sublime Station
chapters.arabic_text:
بالنيات وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى (قال العلماء من أهل اللغة والأصول والفقه

إنما للحصر تفيد تحصيل
# 
# المذكور ونفي ما سواه وقد قدمنا هذا في أول الباب وقد قالوا أنه قيل لأبي

يحيى حبيب بن أبي ثابت التابعي مفتي أهل الكوفة والمعول عليه عندهم رحمه

الله حدثنا عن أشق شيء قال مجيء النية. وعن سفيان الثوري رحمه الله قال ما

عالجت أشد علي من نيتي. وعن يزيد بن  هارون رحمه الله ما عزت النية في

الحديث إلا لشرفها وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال إنما يحفظ الرجل

على قدر نيته. وعن غيره إنما يعطي الناس قدر نياتهم. وعن لإمام أبي عبد

الله محمد بن إدريس الشافعي بالاسناد الصحيح أنه قال وددت أن الخلق تعلموا

هذا على أن لا ينسب إلى حرف منه وقال الشافعي أيضا ما ناظرت أحدا قط على

الغلبة ووددت إذا ناظرت أحدا أن يظهر الحق على يديه. وقال أيضا ما كلمت

أحدا قط إلا أحببت أن يوفق ويسدد ويعاون ويكون عليه رعاية من الله تعالى

وحفظ. وقال الإمام أبو يوسف صاحب أبي حنيفة رحمهما الله تعالى أريدوا

بعلمكم الله تعالى فإني لم أجلس في مجلس قط أنوي فيه أن أتواضع إلا لم أقم

حتى أعلوهم ولم أجلس مجلسا قط أنوي فيه أن أعلوهم إلا لم أقم حتى أفتضح.

# فصل
# وقد ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:) إن

الله تعالى كتب الحسنات والسيئات، فمن هم بحسنة فلم يعملها كتبها الله عنده

حسنة وإن هم بها فعملها كتبها الله عشر حسنات إلى سبعمائة ضعف إلى أضعاف

كثيرة (.
# وثبت في الصحيح أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في الجيش الذين

يقصدون
# 
# الكعبة:) يخسف بأولهم وآخرهم، فقالت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها يا رسول

الله كيف يخسف بأولهم وآخرهم وفيهم أشراف، ومن ليس منهم فقال يخسف بأولهم

وآخرهم ثم يبعثون على نياتهم (.
# وثبت في الصحيحين عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال:) لا هجرة بعد الفتح ولكن جهاد ونية (.
# قلت اختلف أصحابنا وغيرهم من العلماء في معنى لا هجرة بعد الفتح فقيل

معناه لا هجرة من مكة إذ صارت دار إسلام. وقيل لا هجرة بعد الفتح كاملة

الفضل. وأما الهجرة من دار الكفار اليوم فواجبة وجوبا متأكدا على من قدر

عليها إذا لم يقدر على إظهار دين الاسلام هناك فإن قدر  استحب ولا يجب والله

تعالى اعلم وروينا عن السيد الجليل أبي ميسرة عمر بن شرحبيل التابعي الكوفي

الهمذاني باسكان الميم وبالدال المهملة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه كان إذا أخذ

عطاءه تصدق منه فإذا جاء إلى أهله فعده وجدوه سواء فقال لابن أخيه ألا

تفعلون مثل هذا فقالوا لو علمنا أنه لا ينقص لفعلنا قال أبو ميسرة إني لست

أشرط هذا على ربي عز وجل. وقال أمامنا أبو عبد الله محمد بن إدريس الشافعي

رحمه الله خير الدنيا والآخرة في خمس خصال غنى النفس وكف الأذى وكسب الحلال

ولباس التقوى والثقة بالله عز وجل على كل حال وروينا عن السيد الجليل حماد

بن سلمة رحمه الله وكان يعد من الابدال قال من طلب الحديث لغير الله تعالى

مكر به وقال أحمد بن أبي الحواري السيد الجليل في كتاب الزهد الذي صنفه

وسترى ما أنقل من النفائس إن شاء الله تعالى ولم يحصل إلى الآن إسناده ولكن

عندي منه نسخة جيدة محققة
# 
# متقنة ذكر لي بعض أهل العلم والخبرة أنها بخط الدارقطني رحمه الله. قال

أحمد حدثنا إسحاق بن خلف قال حدثنا حفص بن غياث قال كان عبد الرحمن بن

الأسود رضي الله تعالى عنه لا يأكل الخبز إلا بنية قلت لاسحاق وأي شيء

النية في أكل الخبز قال كان يأكل فإذا ثقل عن الصلاة خفف ليخف بها فإذا خفف

ضعف فأكل ليقوى فكان أكله لها وتركه لها قلت معنى يخف أي ينشط وتسهل عليه

ويلتذ بها. وأحمد بن الحواري يقال بفتح الراء وبكسرها والكسر أشهر والفتح

سمعته مرات من شيخنا الحافظ أبي البقاء يحكيه عن أهل الإتقان وعن بعضهم

والله تعالى أعلم.
# وقال أحمد بن أبي الحواري سمعت أبا سليمان يعني الداراني رحمه الله يقول

عاملوا الله بقلوبكم معناه طهروا قلوبكم وصفوها وهذبوها ولا تخلوا شيئا من

الأعمال الظاهرة. والداراني يقال بالقنون بعد الألف الثانية ويقال بهمزة

بدل النون وهو ابلنون أشهر وأكثر استعمالا والهمز أقرب إلى الأصل وهو منسوب

إلى دارنا القرية الكبيرة النفيسة بجانب دمشق وكان أبو سليمان من كبار

العارفين وأصحاب الكرامات الظاهرة والأحوال الباهرة والحكم المتظاهرة واسمه

عبد الرحمن بن أحمد بن عطية وسيمر بك إن شاء الله تعالى جمل ما أنقله عنه

من النفائس وهو أحد متأخري بلادنا دمشق وما حولها رضي الله تعالى عنه قال

ما أدرك ما عندك من أدرك بكثرة صلاة ولا صوم ولكن بسخاء
# 
# النفس وسلامة الصدر والنصح للأمة وقال أمامنا الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه

من أراد أن يقضي الله تعالى له بالخير فليحسن الظن بالناس. أخبرنا شيخنا

الإمام الحافظ أبو البقاء بقراءتي عليه قال أخبرنا الحافظ عبد الغني إجازة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to intend, to purpose, to aim at" — the inward resolve (qaṣd) that precedes action; also "distance" (nawā) as the object of striving.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, niyya is the discriminating faculty that elevates a mere act (fiʿl) into an act of worship (ʿibāda) — it is the locus of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and the measure of reward (thawāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the heart's direction toward an aim; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the act's moral valence — the same deed becomes obedience or disobedience solely by intention.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥaṣr (Restriction) — the particle {«إِنَّمَا»} restricts the predicate to the mentioned subject and negates all else, functioning as a qaṣr of the heart's motive over outward form.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Actions are but by intentions, and every man shall have only that which he intended." The scholars of language, of uṣūl, and of jurisprudence have said: {«إِنَّمَا»} (innamā) effects restriction (ḥaṣr) — it affirms the mentioned thing and negates whatever is other than it. We have already presented this at the beginning of this chapter.

They have related that it was said to Abū Yaḥyā Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, the Successor (tābiʿī), muftī of the people of Kūfa and the one relied upon among them — may God have mercy on him — "Narrate to us the most difficult thing [you have encountered]." He said: "The coming of the intention." And concerning Sufyān al-Thawrī — may God have mercy on him — he said: "I have never struggled with anything more severe upon me than my own intention." And concerning Yazīd ibn Hārūn — may God have mercy on him — he said: "The intention is mentioned in ḥadīth only because of its nobility." And concerning Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — he said: "A man is only preserved according to his intention." And concerning another: "People are only given according to their intentions."

And concerning the Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī — with a sound chain of transmission — that he said: "I wished that the people had learned this [ḥadīth] such that not a single letter of it be attributed to me." Al-Shāfiʿī also said: "I have never debated anyone seeking victory, and I wished, whenever I debated someone, that the truth would appear at his hands." He also said: "I have never spoken to anyone except that I loved that he be granted success, rectitude, and aid, and that he be under God's protection and preservation."

And the Imām Abū Yūsuf, the companion of Abū Ḥanīfa — may God be pleased with them both — said: "Intend by your knowledge the face of God Almighty. For I never sat in any gathering intending therein to humble myself, except that I did not rise until I had surpassed them; and I never sat in any gathering intending therein to surpass them, except that I did not rise until I was exposed in disgrace."

---

**CHAPTER**

It is established in the authentic ḥadīths that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«إِنَّ اللهَ تَعَالَى كَتَبَ الْحَسَنَاتِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ، فَمَنْ هَمَّ بِحَسَنَةٍ فَلَمْ يَعْمَلْهَا كَتَبَهَا اللهُ عِنْدَهُ حَسَنَةً، وَإِنْ هَمَّ بِهَا فَعَمِلَهَا كَتَبَهَا اللهُ عَشْرَ حَسَنَاتٍ إِلَى سَبْعِمِائَةِ ضِعْفٍ إِلَى أَضْعَافٍ كَثِيرَةٍ»} — "Indeed God Almighty has written down the good deeds and the evil deeds. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, God writes it with Him as a complete good deed; and if he intends it and does it, God writes it as ten good deeds up to seven hundred-fold, up to many multiples."

It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said concerning the army that set out against the Kaʿba: {«يُخْسَفُ بِأَوَّلِهِمْ وَآخِرِهِمْ»} — "The earth shall swallow their first and their last." ʿĀʾisha — may God be pleased with her — said: "O Messenger of God, how can the earth swallow their first and their last, when among them are nobles, and those not of them?" He said: {«يُخْسَفُ بِأَوَّلِهِمْ وَآخِرِهِمْ ثُمَّ يُبْعَثُونَ عَلَى نِيَّاتِهِمْ»} — "The earth shall swallow their first and their last, then they shall be resurrected according to their intentions."

It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«لَا هِجْرَةَ بَعْدَ الْفَتْحِ وَلَكِنْ جِهَادٌ وَنِيَّةٌ»} — "There is no emigration after the Conquest, but rather striving (jihād) and intention."

I say: Our companions and other scholars have differed concerning the meaning of "no emigration after the Conquest." It was said: Its meaning is that there is no emigration from Mecca, since it had become an abode of Islam. And it was said: There is no emigration after the Conquest that is complete in virtue. As for emigration from the abode of unbelief today, it is obligatory — an emphatic obligation — upon whoever is able to do it, when he is unable to manifest the religion of Islam therein. But if he is able [to manifest it], it is recommended (mustaḥabb) and not obligatory. And God Almighty knows best.

We have narrated from the noble master Abū Maysara ʿUmar ibn Shuraḥbīl, the Kūfan Successor, al-Hamadhānī — with the sukūn on the mīm and the unpointed dāl — may God be pleased with him, that whenever he took his stipend he would give charity from it, and when he came to his family and counted it, they would find it unchanged. He said to his nephew: "Will you not do likewise?" They said: "If we knew that it would not decrease, we would do so." Abū Maysara said: "I do not stipulate this condition upon my Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

And our Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: "The good of this world and the Hereafter lies in five qualities: richness of the soul (ghinā al-nafs), refraining from harm (kaf al-adhā), earning what is lawful (kasb al-ḥalāl), the garment of piety (libās al-taqwā), and trust in God Almighty in every circumstance (al-thiqa billāh)."

We have narrated from the noble master Ḥammād ibn Salama — may God have mercy on him — and he was counted among the abdāl (substitutes) — that he said: "Whoever seeks ḥadīth for other than God Almighty shall be deceived by it."

And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī, the noble master, said in the book of asceticism (al-Zuhd) which he composed — and you shall see what I transmit of the precious gems, God willing — and its chain of transmission has not reached me until now, but I possess a good, verified, and precise copy of it; some scholars of expertise informed me that it is in the handwriting of al-Dāraquṭnī — may God have mercy on him. Aḥmad said: Isḥāq ibn Khalaf narrated to us, he said: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad — may God be pleased with him — would not eat bread except with an intention. I said to Isḥāq: "And what is the intention in eating bread?" He said: "He would eat, and when he felt heavy for prayer, he would lighten [his food] to become active thereby; and when he became light, he would weaken, so he would eat to gain strength. Thus his eating of it and his abstaining from it were both [by intention]." I say: The meaning of "lighten" (yakhiff) is that he becomes active, and it becomes easy for him, and he takes pleasure in it.

And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī — it is said with the fatḥa on the rāʾ and with the kasra; the kasra is more famous, and the fatḥa I heard multiple times from our teacher, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Baqāʾ, narrating it from the people of precision — and from some of them, and God Almighty knows best.

And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: I heard Abū Sulaymān — meaning al-Dārānī — may God have mercy on him, saying: "Deal with God with your hearts" — its meaning: purify your hearts, clarify them, and refine them, and do not leave any of the outward deeds [unaccompanied by this]. And al-Dārānī — it is said with the qāf and nūn after the second alif, and it is said with a hamza in place of the nūn; the form with the nūn is more famous and more widely used, while the hamza is closer to the root. He is attributed to Dārayyā, the great, precious village on the side of Damascus. Abū Sulaymān was among the greatest of the gnostics (ʿārifīn), possessors of manifest miracles (karāmāt), resplendent states (aḥwāl), and abundant wisdoms. His name was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAṭiyya. A portion of what I transmit from him of precious gems shall pass before you, God willing — and he was among the later figures of our land, Damascus and its environs — may God be pleased with him. He said: "No one has attained what is with you by abundance of prayer or fasting, but rather by generosity of soul (sakhāʾ al-nafs), soundness of breast (salāmat al-ṣadr), and sincere counsel to the community (al-nuṣḥ li-l-umma)."

And our Imām al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said: "Whoever desires that God Almighty decree good for him, let him think well of people."

Our teacher, the Imām, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Baqāʾ informed us, with my reading upon him, he said: The ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Ghanī informed us by permission (ijāza).

chapters.title_en: Section 8 — On Sincerity, Asceticism, and the Visions of the Righteous
chapters.arabic_text:
أخبرنا أبو طاهر السلفي أخبرنا أبو محمد عبد الرحمن بن أحمد الدوني قال

سمعت أبا الحسن علي بن محمد الأسد أبادي أخبرنا علي بن الحسين بن علي

أخبرنا أبو منصور يحيى بن أحمد المروزي قال سمعت أبا العباس أحمد بن منصور

قال سمعت أبا طاهر محمد بن الحسين بن ميمون يقول سمعت أبا موسى هارون بن

موسى يقول قال أبو حاتم محمد بن إدريس سمعت أبا قبيصة يقول رأيت سفيان

الثوري في المنام فقال ما فعل الله تعالى بك فقال:
# نظرت إلى ربي كفاحا فقال لي ... هنيئا رضائي عنك يا ابن سعيد
# لقد كنت قواما إذا أظلم الدجا ... بعبرة مشتاق وقلب عميد
# فدونك فاختر أي قصر أردته ... وزرني فإني منك غير بعيد
# قلت السلفي بكسر السين المهملة وفتح اللام منسوب إلى جده يقال له سلفة

كان هذا الجد مشقوق الشفة فقلب بالفارسية سيه لفة بكسر السين وفتح اللام أي

ذو ثلاث شفاه ثم عربت فقيل سلفة وكان أبو طاهر السلفي أحد حفاظ عصره. وأما

الدوني بضم الدال وإسكان الواو فمنسوب إلى الدون قرية بخراسان من أعمال

الدينورو اما الأسدابادي فمنسوب إلى بني ثور بن عبد مناف بن أد بن طابخة بن

الياس بن مضر بن نزار بن معد بن عدنان. وأما قوله نظرت إلى ربي كفاحا فهو

بكسر الكاف ومعناه  معاينة من غير حجاب ولا رسول وقوله إذا أظلم الدجا هو

الظلام وقوله عميد أي محب صادف الحب لله. قال أهل اللغة العميد القلب الذي

هزه العشق.
# أخبرنا شيخنا الإمام الحافظ أبو البقاء رحمه الله أخبرنا أبو محمد عبد

العزيز بن معالي أخبرنا القاضي أبو بكر الخطيب أخبرنا أبو الفتح محمد بن

أحمد بن أبي الفوارس أخبرنا محمد بن أحمد الوراق قال سمعت عبد الله بن سهل

الرازي يقول سمعت يحيى بن معاذ الرازي رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول كم
# 
# من مستغفر ممقوت وساكت مرحوم هذا استغفر الله وقلبه فاجر وهذا ساكت وقلبه

ذاكر. وبالاسناد إلى الخطيب قال حدثنا أبو الحسن الواعظ قال سمعت أبا عبد

الله أحمد بن عطاء الروزبادي رحمه الله يقول من خرج إلى العلم يريد العلم

به نفعه قليل العلم. وبهذا الاسناد قال أبو عبد الله بن عطاء العلم موقوف

على العمل به قلت يعني العلم النافع المطلوب كما قال أمامنا الشافعي رضي

الله تعالى عنه ليس العلم ما حفظ. العلم ما نفع. وأخبرنا شيخنا أبو البقاء

أخبرنا أبو محمد أخبرنا أبو بكر أخبرنا الخطيب أخبرنا علي بن محمود الصوفي

أخبرنا عبد الوهاب بن الحسن الكلابي حدثنا سعيد بن عبد العزيز الحلبي قال

سمعت قاسما الجوعي رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول الدين الورع فأفضل العبادة

مكابدة الليل وأفضل طريق الجنة سلامة الصدر قلت الجوعي بضم الجيم وإسكان

الواو. وقال الإمام الحافظ أبو سعيد السمعاني في كتاب الانساب قاسم الجوعي

هذا له كرامات منسوب إلى الجوع. قال ولعله كان يبقى جائعا كثيرا وأخبرنا

شيخنا أبو البقاء أخبرنا أبو محمد أخبرنا أبو بكر أخبرنا الخطيب أخبرنا

أحمد بن الحسن بن السماك قال سمعت أبا بكر الدقي قال سمعت أبا بكر الزقاق

رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول بني أمرنا هذا على أربع لا نأكل إلا على فاقة ولا

ننام إلا عن غلبة ولا نسكت إلا عن خيفة ولا نتكلم إلا عن وجد قلت الدقي بضم

الدال وإسكان القاف المشددة  وهو من كبار الصوفية وأهل المعارف والكرامات

توفي سنة ستين وثلاثمائة وأما الزقاق فبفتح الزاي وتشديد القاف قال

السمعاني هو نسبة إلى الزق وعمله وبيعه كان أبو بكر الزقاق هذا من كبار

الصوفية أصحاب الكرامات
# 
# الظاهرات والمعارف والمتظاهرات وبهذا الاسناد إلى الزقاق قال كل أحد ينسب

إلى نسب إلا الفقراء فإنهم ينسبون إلى الله عز وجل وكل حسب ونسب ينقطع إلا

حسبهم فإن نسبهم الصدق وحسبهم الفقر. وبلغنا عن الإمام الشافعي رضي الله

تعالى عنه فيما رواه البيهقي رحمه الله بإسناده عن يونس بن عبد الله وقيل

بن عبد الأعلى قال قال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه يا أبا موسى لو اجتهدت

كل الجهد على أن ترضى الناس كلهم فلا سبيل إليه فإن كان كذلك فأخلص عملك

ونيتك لله عز وجل.
# وأخبرنا شيخنا أبو البقاء أخبرنا أبو محمد أخبرنا أبو بكر أخبرنا الخطيب

أخبرنا أحمد بن الحسين الواعظ قال سمعت أبا بكر الطرسوسي يقول سمعت أبا بكر

بن شيبان يقول سمعت أبا عبد الله المغربي يقول صوفي بلا صدق الروزجار أحسن

منه قلت هو براء مضمومة ثم واو ساكنة ثم زاي ثم جيم ثم ألف ثم راء وهو الذي

يعمل في الطين بالمجرفة ونحوها.
# وروينا بأسانيد متعددة عن مقاتل بن صالح الخراساني قال دخلت على حماد بن

سلمة رضي الله تعالى عنه فإذا ليس في البيت بيته إلا حصير وهو جالس عليه

ومصحف يقرأ فيه وجراب فيه علمه ومطهرة يتوضأ فيها فبينا أنا عنده إذ دق داق

الباب فقال يا صبية أخرجي أنظري من هذا قالت هذا رسول محمد بن سليمان قال

قولي له يدخل وحده فدخل وسلم وناوله كتابا فقال اقرأه فإذا فيه بسم الله

الرحمن الرحيم من محمد بن سليمان إلى حماد بن سلمة أما بعد فصبحك الله بما

- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Physical sight, gazing, and perception by the eye; also contemplation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes both sensory vision and intellectual/visionary perception, as in the beatific vision (ru'yat Allāh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for ocular sight; metaphorical (majāz) for insight and dream-vision, as here in the dream of Sufyān al-Thawrī.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The verse "فقال لي ... فقال" sequences a question and answer with the response clause governed by the preceding condition, requiring careful parsing of the dream narrative's chain.
chapters.translation:
I say: Abū Ṭāhir al-Silafī informed us, saying: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad al-Dūnī informed us, saying: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Asadābādī; he informed us: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed us, saying: Abū Manṣūr Yaḥyā ibn Aḥmad al-Marwazī informed us, saying: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr, saying: I heard Abū Ṭāhir Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Maymūn, saying: I heard Abū Mūsā Hārūn ibn Mūsā, saying: Abū Ḥātim Muḥammad ibn Idrīs said: I heard Abū Qabīṣah, saying: I saw Sufyān al-Thawrī in a dream, and he said to me: "What has God, Exalted is He, done with you?" Then he recited:

"I gazed upon my Lord face-to-face, and He said to me: 'Welcome, My pleasure upon you, O son of Saʿīd.
You were steadfast in prayer when darkness deepened, with the tears of a yearning one and a heart deeply smitten.
So take what is yours—choose whichever palace you desire, and visit Me, for I am not far from you.'"

I say: Al-Silafī—with the kasrah on the sīn and fatḥah on the lām—is attributed to his grandfather, called Silafah. This grandfather had a split lip, and in Persian it was rendered "sīh lafah"—with kasrah on the sīn and fatḥah on the lām—meaning "possessor of three lips." Then it was Arabized and said as "Silafah." Abū Ṭāhir al-Silafī was one of the leading memorizers (ḥuffāẓ) of his era. As for al-Dūnī—with ḍammah on the dāl and sukūn on the wāw—it is attributed to Dūn, a village in Khurāsān, in the districts of al-Dīnawar. As for al-Asadābādī, it is attributed to the tribe of Thawr ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Ad ibn Ṭābikhah ibn Ilyās ibn Muḍar ibn Nizār ibn Maʿadd ibn ʿAdnān. As for his saying, "I gazed upon my Lord face-to-face (kifāḥan)"—it is with kasrah on the kāf, and its meaning is direct vision without veil or intermediary. His saying, "when darkness deepened (al-dujā)" means the darkness. His saying, "deeply smitten (ʿamīd)" means a lover whose love is sincerely for God. The linguists say: al-ʿamīd is the heart that love has shaken.

Our teacher, the Imām, the ḥāfiẓ, Abū al-Baqāʾ—may God have mercy on him—informed us, saying: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muʿālī informed us, saying: the judge Abū Bakr al-Khaṭīb informed us, saying: Abū al-Fatḥ Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Fawāris informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Warrāq informed us, saying: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sahl al-Rāzī, saying: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—saying: How many a seeker of forgiveness is detested, and how many a silent one is shown mercy! This one seeks God's forgiveness while his heart is wicked, and that one is silent while his heart is engaged in remembrance (dhikr).

By the same chain to al-Khaṭīb, he said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāʿiẓ narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-Rūdhabārī—may God have mercy on him—saying: Whoever sets out seeking knowledge intending thereby to know God, a little knowledge suffices him. By this same chain, Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: Knowledge is contingent upon acting upon it. I say: He means the beneficial knowledge that is sought, as our Imām al-Shāfiʿī—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—said: "Knowledge is not what is memorized; knowledge is what benefits."

Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ informed us, saying: Abū Muḥammad informed us, saying: Abū Bakr informed us, saying: al-Khaṭīb informed us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Maḥmūd al-Ṣūfī informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḥasan al-Kilābī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥalabī narrated to us, saying: I heard Qāsim al-Jūʿī—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—saying: Religion is scrupulous piety (al-waraʿ); the most excellent act of worship is enduring the night [in prayer]; and the best path to Paradise is soundness of heart. I say: Al-Jūʿī—with ḍammah on the jīm and sukūn on the wāw. The Imām, the ḥāfiẓ, Abū Saʿd al-Samʿānī said in his book al-Ansāb: This Qāsim al-Jūʿī had miracles (karāmāt), and he is attributed to hunger (al-jūʿ). He said: Perhaps he used to remain hungry often.

Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ informed us, saying: Abū Muḥammad informed us, saying: Abū Bakr informed us, saying: al-Khaṭīb informed us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Simmāk informed us, saying: I heard Abū Bakr al-Duqqī, saying: I heard Abū Bakr al-Zaqqāq—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—saying: Our affair is built upon four [principles]: we eat only when in need, we sleep only when overcome [by drowsiness], we remain silent only out of fear, and we speak only out of spiritual ecstasy (wajd). I say: Al-Duqqī—with ḍammah on the dāl and sukūn on the emphatic qāf—he was among the great Sufis and people of spiritual knowledge and miracles; he died in the year 360 [AH]. As for al-Zaqqāq—with fatḥah on the zāy and tashdīd on the qāf—al-Samʿānī said: It is an attribution to the water-skin (ziqq), its making and selling. This Abū Bakr al-Zaqqāq was among the great Sufis, possessors of manifest miracles and abundant spiritual knowledge.

By this same chain to al-Zaqqāq, he said: Everyone is attributed to a lineage, except the poor (fuqarāʾ), for they are attributed to God, Mighty and Majestic. Every lineage and noble descent is cut off, except theirs—for their lineage is truthfulness and their nobility is poverty.

It has reached us from the Imām al-Shāfiʿī—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—in what al-Bayhaqī—may God have mercy on him—narrated with his chain from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd Allāh—and it is said: ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā—who said: Al-Shāfiʿī—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—said: O Abū Mūsā, if you exerted your utmost effort to please all people, you would find no way to it. Since that is so, then make your deeds and your intention sincerely for God, Mighty and Majestic.

Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ informed us, saying: Abū Muḥammad informed us, saying: Abū Bakr informed us, saying: al-Khaṭīb informed us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Wāʿiẓ said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṭarsūsī, saying: I heard Abū Bakr ibn Shaybān, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Maghribī, saying: A Sufi without truthfulness—the mud-worker (al-rūzajār) is better than him. I say: It is with ḍammah on the rāʾ, then sukūn on the wāw, then zāy, then jīm, then alif, then rāʾ—he is the one who works in mud with a trowel and the like.

We have narrated through multiple chains from Muqātil ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Khurāsānī, who said: I entered upon Ḥammād ibn Salamah—may God, Exalted is He, be pleased with him—and found in his house nothing but a straw mat upon which he was sitting, a muṣḥaf he was reading from, a leather bag containing his knowledge, and a vessel for ablution. While I was with him, someone knocked at the door. He said: "O girl, go out and see who this is." She said: "It is the messenger of Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān." He said: "Tell him to enter alone." He entered, greeted, and handed him a letter. He said: "Read it." In it was: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān to Ḥammād ibn Salamah. To proceed: May God grant you a morning of..."

chapters.title_en: Section 9 — On Precious Inherited Sayings and the Etiquette of Seeking Knowledge
chapters.arabic_text:
صبح به أولياءه وأهل طاعته وقعت مسألة فانا نسألك فيها فقال يا صبية هلمي

بالدواة ثم قال اكتب في ظهر الكتاب.
# 
# اما بعد: فأنت صبحك بما صبح به أولياءه  وأهل طاعته أدركنا العلماء وهم لا

يأتون أحدا فإن وقعت مسألة فائتنا فتسألنا عما بدا لك وأن أتيتني فلا تأتني

إلا وحدك ولا تأتني بخيلك ورجلك فلا أنصحك ولا أنصح نفسي والسلام. فبينا

أنا عنده جالس إذ دق داق الباب فقال يا صبية أخرجي انظري من هذا فقال محمد

بن سليمان قال قولي له يدخل وحده فسلم ثم جلس بين يديه فقال مالي إذا نظرت

إليك امتلأت رعبا فقال حماد سمعت ثابتا يعني البناني يقول سمعت أنس بن مالك

رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول العالم

إذا أراد بعلمه وجه الله تعالى هابه كل شيء وإذا أراد يكثر به الكنوز هاب

من كل شيء فقال ما تقول يرحمك الله في رجل له ابنان وهو عن أحدهما أرضى

فأراد أن يجعل له في حياته ثلثي ماله فقال لا ويرحمك الله فإني سمعت ثابتا

البناني يقول أنس بن مالك يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن

الله عز وجل إذا أراد أن يعذب عبدا بماله وفقه عند موته لوصية جائرة. قال

فحاجة قال هات ما لم تكن رزية في دين الله قال أربعين ألف درهم تستعين بها

على ما أنت عليه قال أرددها على من ظلمته بها قال والله ما أعطيتك إلا ما

ورثته قال لا حاجة لي فيها قال اروها عني روى الله عنك أوزارك قال فغير هذا

قال هات ما لم يكن رزية في دين الله قال تأخذها فتقسمها قال فلعلي إن عدلت

في قسمتها أن يقول بعض من لم يرزق منها أنه لم يعدل في قسمتها فيأثم اروها

عني روى الله عنك أوزارك قلت ما أحسن
# 
# هذه الحكاية وما أحسن فوائدها وما جمعت من النفائس والتنبيه على قواعد

مهمة وهي بارزة لا تحتاج إلى التنصيص عليها ولكن فيها أحرف من اللغة نضبطها

وإن كانت معروفة صيانة لها. فقوله ومصحف يقرأ فيه يقال مصحف بضم الميم

وكسرها وفتحها ثلاث لغات  الضم أفصح وقد أوضحتها وبينت أصولها واشتقاقها في

كتاب تهذيب الأسماء واللغات. وقوله جراب هو بكسر الجيم وفتحها لغتان والكسر

أجود. وقوله مطهرة هي بكسر الميم وفتحها لغتان وهي كالإبريق والركوة

وغيرهما مما يتطهر به. وقوله هلمي بمعنى اعطيني وهذه إحدى اللغتين والأخرى

هلم للرجل والمرأة والمثنى والمجموع وهي أفصح وبها جاء القرآن قال الله عز

وجل (هلم شهداءكم) و (هلم الينا) وقوله هات هو بكسر التاء بلا خلاف. أخبرنا

شيخنا الحافظ أبو البقاء بقراءتي عليه أخبرنا الحافظ عبد الغني اجازة

أخبرنا محمد بن عبد الباقي أخبرنا أبو الحسن علي بن محمد الخطيب أخبرنا أبو

الحسين علي بن محمد بن بشران أخبرنا الحسين بن صفوان حدثنا عبد الله بن

محمد حدثني أبو عبد الله التميمي عن أبيه قال رأيت حماد بن سلمة في النوم

فقلت ما فعل بك ربك قال خيرا قلت ماذا قال قال لي طالما كدت نفسك فاليوم

أطيل راحتك وراحة المتعوبين من أجلي بخ بخ ماذا أعددت لهم.
#

| باب في نفائس مأثورة
# روينا في صحيح البخاري رحمه الله قال قال عمار رضي الله عنه في هذه

الكلمات ثلاث من جمعهن فقد جمع الإيمان الانصاف من نفسك وبذل السلام للعالم

والانفاق في الاقتار.
# قلت قد جمع رضي الله عنه في هذه الكلمات خيرات الآخرة والدنيا وعلى هذه

مدار الاسلام لأن من أنصف من نفسه فيما الله تعالى وللخلق عليه ولنفسه من

نصيحتها أو صيانتها فقد بلغ الغاية في الطاعة وقوله بذل السلام للعالم هو

بفتح اللام يعني الناس والتكبر عليهم الارتفاع فوقهم يعني للناس كلهم لقول

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم) وتقرأ السلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف (وهذه من

أعظم مكارم الأخلاق. وهو متضمن للسلامة من العداوات والأحقاد واحتقار الناس

والتكبر عليهم والارتفاع فوقهم وأما الانفاق من الاقتار فهو الغاية في

الكرم وقد مدح الله سبحانه وتعالى على ذلك فقال تعالى ويؤثرون على أنفسهم

ولو كان بهم خصاصة. وهذا عام في نفقة الرجل على عياله وضيفه 
# 
# والسائل منه وكل نفقة في طاعة الله عز وجل. وهو متضمن للتوكل على الله

تعالى والاعتماد على سعة فضله والثقة بضمان الرزق. ويتضمن أيضا الزهد في

الدنيا وعدم إدخار متاعها وترك الاهتمام بشأنها والتفاخر والتكاثر بها

ويتضمن غير ما ذكرته من الخيرات لكني أؤثر في هذا الكتاب الاختصار البليغ

خوفا من الملل. وقد روينا هذه الكلمات في شرح السنة للبغوي عن عمار عن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والله أعلم.
# روينا في صحيح مسلم رحمه الله قال حدثنا يحيى بن يحيى قال أخبرنا عبد

الله بن أبي يحيى بن أبي كثير قال سمعت أبي يقول لا يستطاع العلم براحة

الجسم.
# وروينا في صحيح البخاري رضي الله تعالى عنه قال قال ربيعة يعني شيخ مالك

بن أنس الإمام رضي الله تعالى عنهما لا ينبغي لمن عنده شيء من العلم أن

يضيع نفسه قلت في معنى كلام ربيعة قولان أوضحتهما في شرح صحيح البخاري

واختصرتهما هنا أحدهما معناه من كانت فيه نجابة في العلم وحصل طرفا منه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "morning" or "to come upon someone in the morning"; figuratively, to greet or bless with something at dawn.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes the divine favor bestowed upon the awliyā' (friends of Allah) as an act of grace (faḍl), not merit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is the time of dawn; metaphorical (majāz) here is the spiritual illumination or blessing granted to the pious.
- Root: ه-ل-م (h-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A verbal noun meaning "come" or "bring"; used as an imperative for approaching or giving.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, it functions as a command to "bring forth" witnesses or evidence, as in {«هلم شهداءكم»}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The form "هلمّ" is indeclinable and used for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine alike—considered the more eloquent (afṣaḥ) variant; "هلمي" is a lesser-used feminine singular form.
- Root: ه-ي-ب (h-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is awe, fear, or reverence mixed with veneration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, it is the reverential fear (khashyah) that creatures feel toward a true scholar who acts for Allah's sake—a sign of divine majesty (jalāl) reflected in the scholar.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is fear of a predator or tyrant; metaphorical is the spiritual awe inspired by piety and knowledge, as in the hadith cited.
- Root: ق-ت-ر (q-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Means scarcity, poverty, or tightness of means; the opposite of abundance (saʿah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, it denotes constriction of provision (rizaq) as a divine test; spending during such times is the peak of generosity (karam).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is narrowness of livelihood; metaphorical is spending despite one's own need, as in {«ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة»}.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When a noun follows another without a conjunction to clarify it, as in "محمد بن سليمان" after "من هذا," the second noun specifies the first, requiring no repetition of the verb.
chapters.translation:
I say: He greeted him with morning blessings as He greets His friends and obedient servants. A question arose, and we ask you concerning it. He said: "O young girl, bring me (hilmī) the inkwell." Then he said: "Write on the back of the letter."

To proceed: You have been greeted with morning blessings as He greets His friends and obedient servants. We encountered the scholars, and they did not go to anyone. So if a question arises, come to us and ask us about whatever appears to you. And if you come to me, do not come except alone—do not come with your cavalry and infantry—for then I would not advise you, nor would I advise myself. Peace.

While I was sitting with him, someone knocked at the door. He said: "O young girl, go out and see who this is." He said: "It is Muhammad ibn Sulaymān." He said: "Tell him to enter alone." He greeted, then sat before him and said: "Why is it that when I look at you, I am filled with terror?" Ḥammād said: I heard Thābit—meaning al-Bunānī—say: I heard Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: "When the scholar intends by his knowledge the Face of Allah Most High, everything fears him; and when he intends to amass treasures by it, he fears everything."

He said: "What do you say, may Allah have mercy on you, concerning a man who has two sons, and he is more pleased with one of them, and he wishes to give him two-thirds of his wealth during his lifetime?" He said: "No, and may Allah have mercy on you, for I heard Thābit al-Bunānī say: Anas ibn Mālik said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: 'Indeed, Allah Almighty, when He wishes to punish a servant through his wealth, He withholds from him at his death the ability to make a just will.'"

He said: "Then I have a need." He said: "Bring it, as long as it is not a calamity in the religion of Allah." He said: "Forty thousand dirhams to aid you in what you are upon." He said: "Return it to those whom you have wronged by it." He said: "By Allah, I only gave you what I inherited." He said: "I have no need of it. Narrate it from me—may Allah absolve you of your burdens." He said: "Then something else." He said: "Bring it, as long as it is not a calamity in the religion of Allah." He said: "Take it and distribute it." He said: "Perhaps if I am just in its distribution, someone who received none of it will say that I was not just in its distribution, and thus sin. Narrate it from me—may Allah absolve you of your burdens."

I say: How excellent is this anecdote, and how excellent are its benefits, and what precious gems it contains, and its indication of important principles! They are evident and need no explicit elaboration. However, it contains some lexical points which we shall fix, even though they are known, as a safeguard.

His saying "muṣḥaf" (codex) in which one recites: It is said "muṣḥaf" with ḍammah on the mīm, kasrah on it, and fatḥah on it—three dialects. The ḍammah is the most eloquent. I have clarified this and explained its origins and derivation in my book Tahdhīb al-Asmā' wa al-Lughāt.

His saying "jirāb" (bag): It is with kasrah on the jīm and fatḥah on it—two dialects; the kasrah is better.

His saying "miṭharah" (water vessel for purification): It is with kasrah on the mīm and fatḥah on it—two dialects. It is like the ewer (ibrīq) and the small leather vessel (rakwah) and similar things used for purification.

His saying "hilmī" means "give me." This is one of the two dialects; the other is "halumma" for the man, the woman, the dual, and the plural—and it is the more eloquent, and with it the Quran came. Allah Almighty said: {«هلم شهداءكم»} (Bring your witnesses) and {«هلم إلينا»} (Come to us).

His saying "hāt" (give): It is with kasrah on the tā' without dispute.

Our teacher, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Baqā', informed us, with my reading to him: The ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Ghanī informed us by permission (ijāzah): Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī informed us: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Khaṭīb informed us: Abū al-Ḥusayn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Bishrān informed us: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Ṣafwān narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us: Abū ʿAbdullāh al-Tamīmī narrated to me from his father, who said: I saw Ḥammād ibn Salamah in a dream and said: "What did your Lord do with you?" He said: "Good." I said: "What did He say?" He said: "He said to me: 'How long you wearied yourself for My sake! Today I prolong your rest and the rest of those who wearied themselves for My sake.' Bravo, bravo! What have I prepared for them!"

Chapter on Precious Inherited Sayings

We narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: ʿAmmār, may Allah be pleased with him, said concerning these words: "Whoever gathers three things has gathered faith: fairness to oneself, spreading peace to the world, and spending in times of scarcity."

I say: He, may Allah be pleased with him, has gathered in these words the goods of the Hereafter and this world, and upon these the foundation of Islam rests. For whoever is fair to himself regarding what Allah Most High and the creatures have claim upon him, and regarding his own soul—whether in advising it or safeguarding it—has reached the utmost in obedience.

His saying "spreading peace to the world" (badhl al-salām lil-ʿālam): It is with fatḥah on the lām, meaning the people, and "the world" here means all people, due to the Prophet's saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "And spread peace upon those you know and those you do not know." This is among the greatest noble character traits. It entails safety from enmities and grudges, and from despising people, arrogance toward them, and elevating oneself above them.

As for "spending in times of scarcity" (al-infāq min al-iqtār), it is the utmost in generosity. Allah, glorified and exalted, has praised this, saying: {«ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة»} (And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in need). This is general, covering a man's spending on his family and his guest, and the one who asks of him, and every expenditure in obedience to Allah Almighty.

It entails trust in Allah Most High, reliance on the vastness of His bounty, and confidence in His guarantee of provision. It also entails asceticism (zuhd) in this world, not hoarding its goods, abandoning concern for its affairs, and refraining from boasting and multiplying wealth by it. It entails other goods beyond what I have mentioned, but I prefer in this book eloquent brevity, fearing tedium.

We have also narrated these words in Sharḥ al-Sunnah of al-Baghawī, from ʿAmmār, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And Allah knows best.

We narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr informed us: I heard my father say: "Knowledge is not attained with bodily ease."

We narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said: Rabīʿah—meaning the teacher of Mālik ibn Anas, the Imām, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both—said: "It is not fitting for one who possesses some knowledge to waste himself."

I say: Concerning the meaning of Rabīʿah's words, there are two interpretations, which I have clarified in my commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, and I have summarized them here. One of them is: Whoever has aptitude in knowledge and has obtained a portion of it...

chapters.title_en: Section 10 — On the Marks of Excellence in the Student of Knowledge, the Obligation to Perfect and Disseminate It, and Admonitions on Sincerity, Humility, and Asceticism
chapters.arabic_text:
وظهرت فيه أمارات التبريز فيه فينبغي له أن أن يجتهد في تتمته ولا يضيع

طلبه فيضع نفسه والثاني معناه من حصل له العلم ينبغي له أن يسعى في نشره

مبتغيا به رضا الله تعالى ويشيعه في الناس لينتقل عنه وينتفع به الناس

وينتفع هو وينبغي أن يرفق في نشره بمن يأخذه منه ويسهل طرق أخذ ليكون أبلغ

في نصيحة العلم فإن الدين النصيحة.
# وقد اختلف أصحاب الشافعي رحمه الله وإياهم فيمن كان بالصفة المذكورة في

الأول هل يتعين عليه تتميم الطلب ويحرم الترك أم يبقى في حقه فرض كما كان

فلا يحرم عليه الترك إذا قام به غيره وهذا الثاني هو قول أكثرهم وهو الصحيح

المختار والله أعلم.
# وروينا عن عمر بن الخطاب وابنه عبد الله رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال من رق

وجهه رق علمه. ومعناه من استحيا في طلب العلم كان علمه رقيقا أي قليلا.
# 
# وروينا في صحيح البخاري رضي الله تعالى عنه  قال قال مجاهد رحمه الله لا

يتعلم العلم مستحي ولا متكبر.
# وروينا في صحيح مسلم وغيره عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت نعم النساء

نساء الأنصار لم يكن يمنعهن الحياء أن يتفقهن في الدين.
# وروينا في صحيح البخاري قال قال عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه تفقهوا قبل أن

تسودوا ومعناه أحرصوا على إتقان العلم والتمكن في تحصيله وأنتم شبان لا

أشغال لكم ولا رئاسة ولا سن فإنكم إذا كبرتم وصرتم سادة متبوعين امتنعتم من

التفقه والتحصيل وهذا نحو ما قال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه تفقه قبل أن

ترأس فإذا رأست فلا سبيل إلى التفقه. أخبرنا شيخنا أبو البقاء أخبرنا أبو

محمد أخبرنا أبو بكر أخبرنا الخطيب أخبرنا أبو محمد الأصبهاني حدثنا جعفر

الخالدي قال سمعت الجنيد رحمه الله يقول ما أحب أن أموت حيث أعرف أخاف أن

لا تقبلني الأرض وافتضح بهذا الاسناد قال الجنيد سمعت سريا يقول إني لأنتظر

إلى أنفي كل يوم مرتين مخافة أن يكون قد اسود وجهي.
# وبهذا الإسناد إلى الخطيب قال حدثنا علي بن القاسم قال سمعت الحسين بن

أرجك يقول من خير المواهب العقل ومن شر المصائب الجهل. وبالإسناد إلى

الخطيب قال أخبرنا عبد العزيز حدثنا محمد قال سمعت أبا عبد الله محمد بن

عبد الله تلميذ بشر بن الحارث قال سمعت ابن الحارث رضي الله عنه يقول كانوا

لا يأكلون تلذذا ولا يلبسون تنعما قال وهذا طريق الآخرة والأنبياء

والصالحين ومن بعدهم فمن زعم أن الأمر في غير هذا فهو مفتون. وبالإسناد إلى

الخطيب قال: أخبرنا عبد الرحمن بن محمد النيسابوري حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله

بن بهلول الفقيه حدثنا أحمد بن علي بن
# 
# أبي حمير قال سمعت سهل بن عبد الله رحمه الله يقول حرام على قلب أن يشم

رائحة اليقين وفيه سكون إلى غير الله تعالى وحرام على قلب أن يدخله النور

وفيه شيء مما يكرهه الله تعالى. وبالإسناد إلى الخطيب قال أخبرنا أبو الحسن

أحمد بن محمد الأهوازي  حدثنا أبو عبد الله محمد بن مخلد العطار حدثنا موسى

بن هارون حدثنا محمد يعني ابن نعيم بن هصيم قال سمعت بشر هو ابن الحارث

رحمه الله يقول: أوحى الله تعالى إلى داود صلى الله عليه وسلم يا داود لا

تجعل بيني وبينك عالما مفتونا فيصدك بسكره عن طريق محبتي أولئك قطاع طريق

عبادي نسأل الله العافية أخبرنا شيوخنا الثلاثة الأئمة القاضي الإمام بقية

المشايخ أبو الفضل عبد الكريم بن القاضي أبي القاسم عبد الصمد بن محمد

الأنصاري والإمام الحافظ أبو البقاء خالد بن يوسف والشيخ الإمام أبي عبد

الله محمد بن عبد المحسن بن محمد بن منصور الأنصاري الدمشقيون قال أخبرنا

الشيخ الإمام أبو اليمن زيد بن الحسن الكندي أخبرنا أبو بكر محمد بن عبد

الباقي الأنصاري أخبرنا أبو إسحاق بن عمر بن أحمد البرمكي أخبرنا أبو محمد

عبد الله بن إبراهيم بن ناشي أخبرنا أبو مسلم إبراهيم بن عبد الله الكحي

حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله الأنصاري حدثنا سليمان التيمي عن أبي عثمان النهدي

عن سلمان رضي الله تعالى عنه قال لا يعلم الناس عون الله بالضعيف ما عالوا

بالظهر. وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه. عليك بالزهد فالزهد على الزاهد

أحسن من الحلى على الناهد. وقال الربيع رحمه الله تعالى قال لي الشافعي رضي

الله عنه يا ربيع فيما لا يعنيك فإنك إذا تكلمت بالكلمة ملكتك ولم تملكها.
# وقال المزني رحمه الله سمعت الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول ليس لأحد

إلا له محب ومبغض فإذا لا بد من ذلك فليكن المرء مع أهل طاعة الله عز وجل.

وروينا عن الحسن بن عمران بن عيينة أن سفيان بن عيينة رضي الله تعالى عنه

قال له بالمزدلفة في آخر حجة حجها قد وافيت هذا الموضع سبعين
# 
# مرة أقول في كل مرة اللهم لا تجعله آخر العهد من هذا المكان وقد استحييت

من الله عز وجل من كثرة ما أسأله فرجع فتوفي في السنة الداخلة. أخبرنا

الشيخ الأمين السيد  أبو الفضل محمد بن محمد بن محمد بن التيمي البكري

بقراءتي عليه بكلاسة جامع دمشق. قال أخبرنا الشيخ أبو حفص عمر بن محمد بن

معمر بن طبرزد قال أخبرنا الحافظ أبو القاسم إسماعيل بن أحمد بن عمر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ر-ز (baraza)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To appear, emerge, become prominent; al-tabrīz denotes excelling and surpassing peers in a craft or science.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Excellence (tabrīz) in knowledge signifies the manifestation of one's acquired virtue, a state obligating further pursuit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical emergence; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the emergence of scholarly distinction.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — "إذا قام به غيره" (if another undertakes it) governs the permissibility of abandoning the communal obligation, parsed as a suspended protasis with an implied apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: And there appear in him the marks of excellence (tabrīz) in it, so it behooves him to strive diligently in completing it and not to waste his pursuit, lest he debase himself. The second [matter]—its meaning is: whoever has attained knowledge, it behooves him to strive in spreading it, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah the Exalted, and to disseminate it among the people so that it may be transmitted from him, and the people benefit from it, and he himself benefits. And he should be gentle in its dissemination toward those who take it from him, and facilitate the paths of learning, for that is more effective in sincere counsel to knowledge—for indeed, religion is sincere counsel (al-nāṣīḥah).

And the companions of al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah have mercy on him and on them—have differed concerning the one who possesses the aforementioned description in the first [matter]: is it incumbent upon him specifically to complete the pursuit, with abandonment being unlawful, or does it remain in his case a communal obligation (farḍ) as it was, such that abandonment is not unlawful for him if another undertakes it? This second view is the saying of the majority of them, and it is the correct and chosen one—and Allah knows best.

And we have related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and his son ʿAbd Allāh—may Allah be well pleased with them both—that he said: "Whose face softens, his knowledge softens." Its meaning: whoever is bashful in seeking knowledge, his knowledge becomes thin—that is, little.

And we have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī—may Allah be well pleased with him—that he said: Mujāhid—may Allah have mercy on him—said: "Knowledge is not learned by the bashful nor by the arrogant."

And we have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim and others, from ʿĀʾishah—may Allah be well pleased with her—that she said: "Excellent are the women of the Anṣār; shyness did not prevent them from acquiring deep understanding (tafaqquh) in religion."

And we have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī that he said: ʿUmar—may Allah be well pleased with him—said: "Acquire deep understanding (tafaqqahū) before you become leaders." Its meaning: be eager to master knowledge and to become firmly established in its acquisition while you are young, having no occupations, no leadership, and no [burden of] age—for when you grow old and become leaders followed [by others], you will be prevented from deep understanding and acquisition. This is similar to what al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah be well pleased with him—said: "Acquire deep understanding before you assume leadership; for when you assume leadership, there is no path to deep understanding."

Our shaykh Abū al-Baqāʾ informed us: Abū Muḥammad informed us: Abū Bakr informed us: al-Khaṭīb informed us: Abū Muḥammad al-Aṣbahānī informed us: Jaʿfar al-Khālidī narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Junayd—may Allah have mercy on him—saying: "I would not love to die in a place where I am known; I fear that the earth would not accept me, and I would be disgraced." And with this chain, al-Junayd said: I heard Sarī [al-Saqaṭī] saying: "Indeed, I look at my nose twice every day, fearing that my face may have blackened."

And with this chain to al-Khaṭīb, he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḥusayn ibn Arjak saying: "Among the best of gifts is intellect, and among the worst of calamities is ignorance."

And with the chain to al-Khaṭīb, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz informed us: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, the disciple of Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith, saying: I heard Ibn al-Ḥārith—may Allah be well pleased with him—saying: "They did not eat for pleasure, nor did they dress for comfort." He said: "And this is the path of the Hereafter, and of the Prophets and the righteous, and those after them. So whoever claims that the matter lies in other than this is deluded (maftūn)."

And with the chain to al-Khaṭīb, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Naysābūrī informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bahlūl al-Faqīh narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥumayr narrated to us, saying: I heard Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh—may Allah have mercy on him—saying: "It is forbidden (ḥarām) for a heart to smell the fragrance of certainty (al-yaqīn) while in it there is repose in other than Allah the Exalted; and it is forbidden for a heart to be entered by light while in it there is something that Allah the Exalted dislikes."

And with the chain to al-Khaṭīb, he said: Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Ahwāzī informed us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Makhlad al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us: Mūsā ibn Hārūn narrated to us: Muḥammad—meaning Ibn Nuʿaym ibn Haṣīm—narrated to us, saying: I heard Bishr—he is Ibn al-Ḥārith—may Allah have mercy on him—saying: "Allah the Exalted revealed to Dāwūd—peace be upon him: 'O Dāwūd, do not place between Me and you a deluded scholar (ʿāliman maftūnan), lest he turn you away by his intoxication from the path of My love. Those are the highway robbers of My servants.'" We ask Allah for well-being.

Our three shaykhs informed us—the judge, the imam, the remnant of the shaykhs, Abū al-Faḍl ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn al-Qāḍī Abī al-Qāsim ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī; and the imam, the ḥāfiẓ, Abū al-Baqāʾ Khālid ibn Yūsuf; and the shaykh, the imam, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Muḥsin ibn Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr al-Anṣārī, all of Damascus—they said: The shaykh, the imam, Abū al-Yaman Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan al-Kindī informed us: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī al-Anṣārī informed us: Abū Isḥāq ibn ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad al-Barmakī informed us: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Nāshī informed us: Abū Muslim Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kaḥḥī narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī narrated to us: Sulaymān al-Taymī narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Salmān—may Allah be well pleased with him—that he said: "People do not know the help of Allah [given] through the weak, [and] what they have neglected by [relying on] the strong."

And al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah be well pleased with him—said: "Upon you is asceticism (al-zuhd), for asceticism upon the ascetic is more beautiful than adornment upon a young woman with a swelling bosom (al-nāhid)."

And al-Rabīʿ—may Allah have mercy on him—said: Al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah be well pleased with him—said to me: "O Rabīʿ, [refrain] from what does not concern you; for when you speak a word, it possesses you, and you do not possess it."

And al-Muzanī—may Allah have mercy on him—said: I heard al-Shāfiʿī—may Allah be well pleased with him—saying: "There is no one who does not have a lover and a hater; and since that is unavoidable, let a man be with the people of obedience to Allah the Mighty and Majestic."

And we have related from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah that Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah—may Allah be well pleased with him—said to him at Muzdalifah, in the last pilgrimage he performed: "I have come to this place seventy times, saying each time: 'O Allah, do not make this the last of my covenant with this place'—and I have become ashamed before Allah the Mighty and Majestic due to the frequency of my asking Him." Then he returned and died in the following year.

Our shaykh, the trustworthy one, the sayyid, Abū al-Faḍl Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Taymī al-Bakrī informed us, by my reading to him at Kalāsah in the Jāmiʿ of Damascus. He said: The shaykh Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn Muʿammar ibn Ṭabarzad informed us. He said: The ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim Ismāʿīl ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar informed us...

chapters.title_en: The Vision of Abu Sulayman al-Darani and the Severity of Scrupulousness (Al-Waraʿ) in Minor Transgressions
chapters.arabic_text:
السمرقندي قال سمعت عبد الدائم بن الحسن الهلالي يقول سمعت عبد الوهاب بن

الحسن الكلابي يقول سمعت محمد بن خريم العقيلي يقول سمعت أحمد بن أبي

الحواري يقول تمنيت أن أرى أبا سليمان الداراني رحمه الله في المنام فرأيته

بعد سنة فقلت يا معلم ما فعل الله بك فقال يا محمد جئت من باب الصغير فلقيت

وسق شيخ فأخذت منه عودا ما أدري تخللت به أو رميت به فأنا في حسابه منذ سنة

إلى هذه الليلة قلت ما أبلغ هذه الحكاية في الحث على الورع والتحذير من

التساهل في محقرات المظالم، والوسق بفتح الواو وبكسرها لغتان وهو الحمل،

ومعمر المذكور بضم الميم الأول وفتح الثانية وتشديدها، وخريم بضم الخاء

وبالراء، والعقيلي بضم العين. أخبرنا شيخنا الإمام الصالح الحافظ المتقن

أبو إسحاق إبراهيم بن عيسى بن يوسف المرادي بقراءتي عليه قال أخبرنا الشيخ

الإمام أبو الحسن بن هبة الله الحميري أخبرنا الحافظ أبو طاهر السلفي،

أخبرنا الإمام أبو بكر أحمد بن محمد بن أحمد بن محمد بن زنجويه أخبرنا أبو

طالب يحيى بن علي الدسكري قال سمعت أبا أحمد الغطريفي يقول سمعت أبا العباس

محمد بن إسحاق السراج يقول سمعت عبد الله بن محمد الوراق يقول مروا بمعروف

أيام الفتنة يتقاتلون وهو يقول لهم مروا أصحبكم الله مروا بارك الله فيكم

فقيل له إنهم يخرجون عن القتال فقال إن أصحبهم الله لم يقاتلوا.
# 
# أخبرنا شيخنا أبو إسحاق بهذا الاسناد إلى السراج قال سمعت ابن أبي الدنيا

يقول جلس إلى معروف فاغتاب رجل منهم رجلا فقال يا هذا اذكر يوم يوضع القطن

على عينيك، وبهذا الإسناد قال السراج سمعت يحيى بن أبي طالب يقول سمعت

يعقوب بن أخي معروف يقول سمعت عمي يقول كلاما فيما  لا يعنيه خذلان من الله

تعالى. وبهذا الاسناد قال السراج سمعت علي بن الموفق يقول كان من دعاء

معروف يا مالك يا قدير يا من ليس له نظير. وبهذا الإسناد إلى الغطريفي بن

أدهم بالشام فقلت ما أقدمك ها هنا فقال أما إني لم أقدمها لجهاد ولا لرباط

ولكن قدمتها لأشبع من خبز حلال. وروينا عن الحافظ أحمد بن عبد الله العجلي

قال ربعي بن خراش تابعي ثقة لم يكذب قط كان له ابنان عاصيان زمن الحجاج

فقيل للحجاج إن أباهما لم يكذب قط لو أرسلت إليه فسألته عنهما فأرسل إليه

فقال أين ابناك فقال هما في البيت فقال قد عفونا عنهما بصدقك وقال الحارث

الغزي آلى ربيع بن خراش أن لا يصير ضاحكا حتى يعلم أين مصيره فما ضحك إلا

بعد موته وآلى أخوه ربعي بعده أن لا يضحك حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أو في

النار. قال الحارث ولقد أخبرني غاسله أنه لم يزل متبسما على سريره ونحن

نغسله حتى فرغنا من غسله.
# وروينا عن أحمد بن عبد الله قال اجتمع قراء أهل الكوفة في منزل الحكم بن

عتيبة فأجمعوا على أن أقرأ أهل الكوفة طلحة بن مصرف فبلغه ذلك فقعد إلى

الأعمش يقرأ عليه ليذهب لذلك الاسم عنه. قلت عتيبة بتاء مثناة من فوق ثم

ياء مثناة من تحت ثم باء موحدة ومصرف بضم الميم وفتح الصاد المهملة وكسر

الراء المشددة على المشهور. وقيل بفتح الراء. وعن الإمام الشافعي رحمه الله

قال قيل لأبي بن كعب رضي الله تعالى عنه يا أبا المنذر عظني قال وأخي

الاخوان على قدر تقواهم ولا تجعل لسانك بدأت
# 
# لمن لا يرغب فيه ولا تغبط الحي إلا بما تغبط به الميت. وعن الشافعي رحمه

الله قال قال فضيل بن عياض رضي الله تعالى عنه كم ممن يطوف بهذا البيت وآخر

بعيد منه وأعظم أجرا منه. وعن الشافعي عن فضيل قال قال داود النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم إلهي كن لابني كما كنت  لي فأوحى الله تعالى إليه يا داود قل

لابنك يكن لي كما كنت لي أكون له كما كنت لك. وعن الشافعي رحمه الله قال

قال هشام بن عبد الملك ارفع حاجتك إلي فقال قد رفعتها إلى الجواد الكريم.

وروينا في رسالة القشيري رحمه الله في باب كرامات الأولياء قال كان لجعفر

الخلدي فص فوقع يوما في دجلة وكان عنده دعاء مجرب للضالة ترد فدعا به فوجد

الفص في وسط أوراق كان يتصفحها. قال القشيري سمعت أبا حاتم السجستاني يقول

سمعت أبا نصر السراج يقول إن ذلك الدعاء يا جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه

اجمع على ضالتي. قلت وقد جربت هذا الدعاء فوجدته نافعا سببا لوجود الضالة

على قرب غالبا وأنه لم ينخرم. وسمعت شيخنا أبا البقاء يقول نحو ذلك وهو

علمنيه أولا قول فص هو بفتح الفاء وكسرها لغتان الفتح أجود. وأما جعفر

الخلدي هو بضم الخاء المعجمة وإسكان اللام قال الحافظ الإمام أبو سعيد

السمعاني في الأنساب الخلد محلة ببغداد ينسب إليها صبيح الراوي عن عثمان بن

عفان وعائشة رضي الله تعالى عنهما. قال وأما جعفر بن محمد بن نصر الخلدي

الخواص أبو محمد أحد مشايخ الصوفية له كرامات ظاهرة وإنما قيل له الخلدي

لأنه كان يوما عند الجنيد فسأل يوما على مسألة فقال الجنيد أجبهم فأجابهم

فقال له الجنيد من أين لك هذه الأجوبة فقال من خلدي فبقي عليه هذا الاسم

حتى توفي سنة ثمان وأربعين وثلثمائة روى عنه الدارقطني وأبو حفص بن شاهين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-ع (W-R-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is abstention and avoidance; al-waraʿ is the restraint of the soul from what is doubtful or forbidden, rooted in the sense of shrinking back (tawarruʿ) from impurity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, it is the highest station of piety (taqwā) where one abandons even permissible things (mubāḥāt) out of fear of falling into the prohibited; it is a safeguard for the heart's purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it denotes physical withdrawal; metaphorically (majāz), it signifies the soul's retreat from moral and legal ambiguities (shubuhāt), as exemplified in the narrative of the date-stick.
- Root: ح-س-ب (Ḥ-S-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To count, reckon, or account; the act of enumeration and calculation of deeds.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, it refers to the divine reckoning (ḥisāb) on the Day of Judgment, where every atom of action is weighed, including the seemingly trivial.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal counting of objects; metaphorical application to the moral audit of one's life, where even a discarded twig becomes a matter of prolonged accountability.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "فأنا في حسابه منذ سنة" employs a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya) to denote a continuous state, emphasizing the enduring nature of the reckoning, which is a stylistic choice for permanence over the verbal form.
chapters.translation:
I say: Al-Samarqandi said: I heard ʿAbd al-Dāʾim ibn al-Ḥasan al-Hilālī say: I heard ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn al-Ḥasan al-Kilābī say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Khuraym al-ʿUqaylī say: I heard Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī say: I wished to see Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī (may Allah have mercy on him) in a dream, and I saw him after a year. I said: O teacher, what has Allah done with you? He said: O Muḥammad, I came from the Small Gate (Bāb al-Ṣaghīr) and met a camel-load (wasq) of an old man. I took from it a stick—I do not know whether I used it as a toothpick or threw it away—and I have been in its reckoning for a year until this very night. I say: How profound is this narrative in urging scrupulousness (al-waraʿ) and warning against leniency in the minor aspects of injustices (maẓālim). The word "wasq" is pronounced with fatḥa on the wāw or kasra on it—two dialects—and it means a camel-load. The aforementioned Muʿammar is with ḍamma on the first mīm and fatḥa on the second with tashdīd. Khuraym is with ḍamma on the khāʾ and with rāʾ. Al-ʿUqaylī is with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

Our teacher, the righteous Imam, the precise memorizer (al-ḥāfiẓ al-mutqin), Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn ʿĪsā ibn Yūsuf al-Murādī, informed us, with my recitation upon him, saying: The Imam Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Hibat Allāh al-Ḥimyarī informed us: The memorizer Abū Ṭāhir al-Silafī informed us: The Imam Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Abū Ṭālib Yaḥyā ibn ʿAlī al-Daskarī informed us, saying: I heard Abū Aḥmad al-Ghiṭrīfī say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sarrāj say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Warrāq say: They passed by Maʿrūf during the days of civil strife (fitna) while they were fighting, and he was saying to them: "Pass on, may Allah set you right (aṣḥabakum Allāh); pass on, may Allah bless you."
