It was said to him: They are leaving the fighting. He said: If Allah had set them right (aṣḥabahum), they would not have fought.

Our teacher Abū Isḥāq informed us with this chain to al-Sarrāj, who said: I heard Ibn Abī al-Dunyā say: A man sat with Maʿrūf, and one of them backbited another man. He said: O this one, remember the day when cotton will be placed on your eyes. And with this chain, al-Sarrāj said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ṭālib say: I heard Yaʿqūb, the nephew of Maʿrūf, say: I heard my uncle say: Speaking about what does not concern one is an abandonment (khidhlān) from Allah the Exalted. And with this chain, al-Sarrāj said: I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Muwaffaq say: Among the supplications of Maʿrūf was: "O King (Yā Mālik), O All-Powerful (Yā Qadīr), O He who has no equal." And with this chain to al-Ghiṭrīfī: [He said] I came to Ibn Adham in Syria, and I said: What has brought you here? He said: Indeed, I have not come for jihad nor for frontier guarding (ribāṭ), but I have come to satiate myself with lawful bread (khubz ḥalāl).

And we have related from the memorizer Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿIjlī, who said: Ribʿī ibn Khirāsh was a trustworthy follower (tābiʿī) who never lied. He had two disobedient sons during the era of al-Ḥajjāj. It was said to al-Ḥajjāj: Their father has never lied; if you sent for him and asked him about them [he would tell the truth]. So he sent for him and said: Where are your two sons? He said: They are in the house. He said: We have pardoned them due to your truthfulness. And al-Ḥārith al-Ghazzī said: Ribāʿ ibn Khirāsh swore an oath that he would not laugh until he knew his final destination. He did not laugh except after his death. And his brother Ribʿī swore after him that he would not laugh until he knew whether he was in Paradise or the Fire. Al-Ḥārith said: And his washer (ghāsiluhu) informed me that he did not cease smiling on his bier while we were washing him until we finished his washing.

And we have related from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The reciters (qurrāʾ) of Kufa gathered in the house of al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba and agreed that the most proficient reciter of Kufa was Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif. When this reached him, he sat with al-Aʿmash to recite to him, so that this designation would depart from him. I say: ʿUtayba is with a tāʾ with two dots above, then a yāʾ with two dots below, then a bāʾ with one dot. Muṣarrif is with ḍamma on the mīm, fatḥa on the ṣād (unpointed), and kasra on the shaddah'd rāʾ, according to the well-known pronunciation. It is also said with fatḥa on the rāʾ.

And from Imam al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: It was said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him): O Abā al-Mundhir, give us counsel. He said: And I—brothers are upon the measure of their piety (taqwā), and do not make your tongue the beginning for one who does not desire it, and do not envy the living except for that which you would envy the dead for. And from al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him) said: How many are those who circumambulate this House (the Kaʿba), while another is far from it yet greater in reward than him! And from al-Shāfiʿī, from Fuḍayl, who said: Prophet Dāwūd (peace be upon him) said: "My God, be to my son as You were to me." So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "O Dāwūd, say to your son: Be to Me as you were to Me, and I will be to him as I was to you." And from al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said [to a man]: Raise your need to me. He said: I have raised it to the Generous, the Noble (al-Jawād al-Karīm).

And we have related in the Epistle of al-Qushayrī (may Allah have mercy on him), in the chapter on the miracles of the saints (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ), that he said: Jaʿfar al-Khuldī had a ring-stone (faṣṣ) that fell one day into the Tigris. He had a tested supplication for the return of lost items, so he supplicated with it and found the ring-stone in the midst of pages he was leafing through. Al-Qushayrī said: I heard Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī say: I heard Abū Naṣr al-Sarrāj say: That supplication is: "O Gatherer of mankind for a Day in which there is no doubt, gather for me my lost item." I say: I have tested this supplication and found it beneficial as a means for the recovery of lost items, often quickly, and that it has never failed. And I heard our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ say something similar, and he was the one who first taught it to me. The word "faṣṣ" is with fatḥa on the fāʾ or kasra—two dialects, with the fatḥa being more eloquent. As for Jaʿfar al-Khuldī, it is with ḍamma on the khāʾ (pointed) and sukūn on the lām. The memorizer Imam Abū Saʿd al-Samʿānī said in al-Ansāb: "Al-Khuld" is a quarter in Baghdad, to which Ṣubayḥ, the narrator from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and ʿĀʾisha (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), is attributed. He said: As for Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Khuldī al-Khawwāṣ, Abū Muḥammad, one of the Sufi masters, he had manifest miracles. He was only called "al-Khuldī" because one day he was with al-Junayd, and a question was posed. Al-Junayd said: Answer them. So he answered them, and al-Junayd said to him: From where did you get these answers? He said: From my khuld (my innate disposition). So this name remained with him until he died in the year 348 AH. Al-Dāraquṭnī and Abū Ḥafṣ ibn Shāhīn narrated from him.

chapters.title_en: Section 12 — On the Etiquette of Leaving Aside Concern for Fine Dress, Food, and Drink, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
وغيرهما وكان ثقة روى عن الحارث بن أبي أسامة وغيره وقال أحمد بن أبي

الحواري
# 
# في كتاب الزهد سمعت بعض أصحابنا أظنه أبا سليمان يعني الداراني رضي الله

عنه قال لإبليس شيطان يقال له متقاض ابن آدم عشرين سنة ليخبر بعمله الذي

يعمله سرا فيظهر له ليزيح عنه ما بين السر والعلانية وروينا عن إبراهيم بن

سعيد قال قلت لأبي سعد بن إبراهيم بم فاقكم الزهري قال كان يأتي المجالس من

صدورها ولا  يأتيها من خلفها ولا يبقى في المجلس شاب إلا سائله ولا كهل إلا

سائله ولا عجوز ولا فتى إلا سائله ثم يأتي الدار من دور الأنصار فلا يبقي

فيها شاب إلى سائله ولا كهل إلا سائله ولا عجوز إلا سائلها ولا كهلة إلا

سائلها حتى يحاور أرباب الحجول. ومن أحسن ما يتأدب به في ترك الاعتناء بحسن

اللباس والمأكل والمشرب ونحوها ما روينا عن أمير المؤمنين عمر بن الخطاب

رضي الله تعالى عنه بإسنادنا إلى أبي عوانة الاسرايني قال حدثنا أبو حبيب

المصيصي حدثنا حجاج قال سمعت شعبة يحدث عن قتادة قال سمعت أبا عثمان النهدي

رحمه الله قال أتانا كتاب عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه ونحن بأذربيجان

مع عتبة بن فرقد.
# أما بعد فاتزروا وارتدوا وانتعلوا وارموا بالخفاف والقوا السراويلات

وعليكم بلباس أبيكم إسماعيل صلى الله عليه وسلم وإياكم والتنعم وزي العجم

وعليكم
# 
# بالشمس فإنها حمام العرب وتمعدوا وأخشوشنوا واخلولقوا واقطعوا الركب

وارموا الأغراض. قوله اخلولقوا لم أقف على ضبطه ولعلها بالخاء المعجمة من

قول العرب اخلولق السحاب إذا استوى واخلولق الرسم إذا استوى بالأرض. أما

ضبط ألفاظه فالمصيصي بكسر الميم والصاد المشددة ويقال بفتح الميم وتخفيف

الصاد والأول أشهر وأرجح نسبة إلى المصيصة البلدة المعروفة بناحية طرسوس

ببلاد الأرمن وأبو عثمان النهدي بفتح النون وإسكان الهاء منسوب إلى جد له

من أجداده والأول اسمه نهد بن زيد بن ليث. واسم أبي عثمان عبد الرحمن بم مل

بفتح الميم وضمها وكسرها واللام مشددة فيها. ويقال ملء بكسر الميم وإسكان

اللام وبعدها همزة وهو من كبار التابعين المخضرمين وأحدهم مخضرم بفتح الراء

وهو من أدرك الجاهلية. والإسلام وحياة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم

يره صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد بينت هذا القدر من حالة في الإرشاد في علوم

الحديث الذي اختصرته من كتاب الشيخ أبي عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله تعالى.

وكان أبو عثمان رحمه الله عظيم القدر كبير الشأن
# 
# قال بلغت نحوا من ثلاثين ومائة  سنة وما من شيء إلا وقد أنكرته إلا أملي

فإني أجده كما هو. ولما قتل الحسين رضي الله تعالى عنه تحول من الكوفة إلى

البصرة وقال لا أسكن بلدا قتل فيه ابن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مات

سنة خمس وتسعين من الهجرة وقيل سنة مائة رحمه الله بأذربيجان. هو إقليم

معروف. وفي ضبطه وجهان مشهوران أحدهما بإسكان الذال المعجمة من غير مد وفتح

الراء وبعدها باء موحدة مكسورة ثم ياء مثناة من تحت ساكنة ثم جيم والثاني

بمده في أوله وفتح الذال وإسكان الراء وقوله وزي العجم هو بكسر الزاي وقوله

وتمعدوا أي تخلقوا بعادة أبيكم معد بن عدنان في خشونة العيش. واختلف

النحويون في ميم معد هل هي أصلية أم زائدة فقال سيبويه أصلية وغيره يقول

زائدة وقوله أرموا الأغراض أي ارموا بالقسي وقوله وتروا معناه إذا ركبتم

الخيل فبتوا من الأرض ولا ترتفعوا على حدر ونحوه ولا تركبوا بالركب

المعتادة للعجم في سروجهم.
# أخبرنا الشيخ الفقيه المسند أبو محمد عبد الرحمن بن سالم بن يحيى

الأنباري قال أخبرنا الحافظ عبد القادر الزهاوي قال حدثنا القاضي أبو

سليمان داود بن محمد بن الحسين الخالدي قال أخبرنا عمر بن محمد بن أحمد

النسفي أخبرنا الحسن بن عبد الملك أخبرنا الحسين بن محمد بن نعيم أخبرنا

عبد الله بن محمد بن أحمد بن يعقوب أخبرنا الحسن بن سفيان حدثنا محمد بن

مرزوق حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم حدثنا عيسى بن حميد الراسي أبو همام حدثنا أبو

حفص النضر عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري أنه أتى رجلا يسأله عن ستر المؤمن

فقلت لست أنا ذاك ولكن ذاك رجل يقال له شهاب فسار جابر فأتى عاملها يعني

عامل البلدة الوالي رجلا يقال له مسلمة فأتى الباب فقال للبواب قل للأمير

ينزل إلي فدخل البواب وهو مبتسم فقال له الأمير ما شأنك قال رجل على بعير

قال قل للأمير ينزل إلي فقال ألا سألته من هو فرجع فسأله فقال أنا جابر بن

عبد الله الأنصاري فرجع إلى الأمير وأخبره فوثب عن مجلسه فأشرف عليه وقال

اصعد فقال جابر ما أريد أن أصعد ولكن حدثني أين منزل شهاب قال اصعد فأرسل

إليه فيقضي حاجتك فقال لا أريد أن يأتيه
# 
# رسولك فإن رسول الأمير إذا جاء رجلا راعه ذاك وأنا أكره أن يروع رجل من

المسلمين بسببي فنزل الأمير يمشي معه حتى أتى شهابا فأشرف عليهم شهاب فقال

إما أن تصعدوا وإما أن أنزل إليكم قال جابر ما أريد أن تنزل إلينا وما نريد

أن نصعد إليك ولكن حدثنا بحديث سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ه-د (z-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abstinence, renunciation, turning away from something due to its insignificance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Asceticism as a virtue of the soul that diminishes attachment to worldly matters, a station of the righteous.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to abstain"; metaphorically applied to the heart's detachment from worldly adornments.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — used in chains like "أبي سليمان يعني الداراني" where the explicative clause clarifies the antecedent.
chapters.translation:
I say: And among those [narrators] was another, and he was trustworthy; he narrated from al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah and others. Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said — in the Book of Asceticism (Kitāb al-Zuhd) — I heard one of our companions, and I think it was Abū Sulaymān, meaning al-Dārānī, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Iblīs has a devil called "Mutaqāḍī" (the Claimant) who pursues the son of Adam for twenty years to uncover the deed he does in secret, then appears to him, to remove from him what lies between the secret and the open.

And we have narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd, who said: I said to Abū Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm: "By what did al-Zuhrī surpass you?" He said: "He would come to gatherings from their front, not from behind them; and he would not leave any young man in the gathering without questioning him, nor any middle-aged man without questioning him, nor any old woman or youth without questioning him. Then he would go to a house among the houses of the Anṣār, and would not leave any young man in it without questioning him, nor any middle-aged man without questioning him, nor any old woman without questioning her, nor any elderly woman without questioning her — until he had conversed with the masters of the veiled women (arbāb al-ḥujūl)."

And among the finest things by which one is disciplined in leaving aside concern for fine dress, food, drink, and the like, is what we have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him — through our chain of transmission to Abū ʿAwānah al-Asrāyīnī, who said: Abū Ḥabīb al-Miṣṣīṣī narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: I heard Shuʿbah narrating from Qatādah, who said: I heard Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, may Allah have mercy on him, say: The letter of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, came to us while we were in Azerbaijan with ʿUtbah ibn Farqad.

"To proceed: Wear waist-wrappers (itazzarū), and cloaks (irtaddū), and sandals (intalū), and shoot with the bows (irmū bil-khifāf), and cast off the trousers (alqū al-sarāwīlāt). And adhere to the dress of your father Ismāʿīl, peace be upon him. And beware of soft living (al-tanaʿʿum) and the attire of the non-Arabs (zī al-ʿajam). And adhere to the sun, for it is the bathhouse of the Arabs (ḥammām al-ʿArab). And emulate Maʿadd (tamaʿʿadū), and be rough in living (akhshawshanū), and be even and level (ikhlawlaqū), and cut the saddle-straps (iqṭaʿū al-rukab), and shoot at the targets (irmū al-aghrāḍ)."

His saying "ikhlawlaqū" — I have not come across its precise voweling. Perhaps it is with the dotted khāʾ (kh), from the Arabs' saying: "ikhlawlaqa al-saḥāb" (the cloud became level) when it evens out, and "ikhlawlaqa al-rasm" (the trace became level) when it evens out with the ground.

As for the voweling of its words: "al-Miṣṣīṣī" is with kasrah on the mīm and shaddah on the ṣād; and it is also said with fatḥah on the mīm and takhfīf (no shaddah) on the ṣād — and the first is more famous and more preponderant, being a nisbah to al-Miṣṣīṣah, the well-known town in the region of Ṭarsūs in the lands of the Armenians. And Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī — with fatḥah on the nūn and sukūn on the hāʾ — is a nisbah to a grandfather among his forefathers; the first of them was named Nahd ibn Zayd ibn Layth. And the name of Abū ʿUthmān was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mull — with fatḥah, ḍammah, or kasrah on the mīm, and shaddah on the lām in all of them. And it is also said "Milʾ" with kasrah on the mīm and sukūn on the lām, followed by a hamzah. And he was among the great Successors (al-tābiʿīn) who were "mukhaḍramūn" — and one of them is "mukhaḍram" with fatḥah on the rāʾ — meaning one who reached the Jāhiliyyah and Islam and the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, but did not see him, peace be upon him. And I have already explained this much of his condition in my book al-Irshād fī ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth, which I abridged from the book of the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him.

And Abū ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, was of great standing and immense rank. He said: "I reached approximately one hundred and thirty years, and there is nothing I have not come to disapprove of except my hope (amalī), for I find it just as it was." And when al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed, he moved from Kūfah to Baṣrah and said: "I will not dwell in a land in which the son of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was killed." He died in the year ninety-five of the Hijrah, and it is said in the year one hundred, may Allah have mercy on him.

"Azerbaijan" — it is a well-known region. In its voweling there are two famous ways: one is with sukūn on the dhāl (dotted) without madd, and fatḥah on the rāʾ, followed by a bāʾ with kasrah, then a yāʾ (two-dotted from below) with sukūn, then a jīm. The second is with madd at its beginning, fatḥah on the dhāl, and sukūn on the rāʾ.

His saying "wa-zī al-ʿajam" — it is with kasrah on the zāy. His saying "wa-tamaʿʿadū" means: adopt the character of your father Maʿadd ibn ʿAdnān in the roughness of living. And the grammarians differed concerning the mīm of "Maʿadd" — is it original or extra? Sībawayh said it is original, and others say it is extra.

His saying "irmū al-aghrāḍ" means: shoot with the bows (qisiyy). And his saying "wa-tarū" means: when you ride horses, then dismount from the ground and do not rise high upon a hill or the like, and do not ride with the saddles (rukab) customary for the non-Arabs in their saddles.

Our Shaykh, the jurist, the muṣnid, Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim ibn Yaḥyā al-Anbārī informed us, saying: The ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Zāhawī informed us, saying: The judge Abū Sulaymān Dāwūd ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Khālidī narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nasafī informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-Malik informed us: al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Nuʿaym informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaʿqūb informed us: al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Marzūq narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us: ʿĪsā ibn Ḥumayd al-Rāsī, Abū Hammām, narrated to us: Abū Ḥafṣ al-Naḍr narrated to us, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, that he came to a man asking him about the covering of the believer (sitr al-muʾmin). I said: "I am not that one, but that is a man called Shihāb." So Jābir traveled and came to the governor — meaning the governor of the town, the ruler — a man called Maslamah. He came to the door and said to the doorkeeper: "Tell the commander to come down to me." The doorkeeper entered, smiling, and the commander said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "A man upon a camel." He said: "Tell the commander to come down to me." He said: "Why did you not ask him who he was?" So he returned and asked him, and he said: "I am Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī." He returned to the commander and informed him, and he leapt up from his seat, looked down upon him, and said: "Come up." Jābir said: "I do not wish to come up, but tell me where the house of Shihāb is." He said: "Come up, and I will send to him so that he may fulfill your need." He said: "I do not want your messenger to go to him, for when the messenger of the commander comes to a man, that frightens him — and I dislike that a man among the Muslims be frightened because of me." So the commander came down, walking with him, until he came to Shihāb. Shihāb looked down upon them and said: "Either you come up, or I will come down to you." Jābir said: "I do not want you to come down to us, nor do we wish to come up to you — but narrate to us a ḥadīth you heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him."

chapters.title_en: On Concealing a Believer's Faults and the Punishment for Mocking the Sunnah
chapters.arabic_text:
يقول: من ستر على أخيه المؤمن فكأنما أحياه. ومما أنشدوا في اكرام من له

نسبة إلى المحبوب قول بعضهم:
# الا حي الديار بسعد اني ... أحب لحب فاطمة الديارا
# سعد بضم السين المهملة وإسكان العين اسم موضع بنخل قال أبو بكر الهمذاني

في كتاب الاشتقاق أصله سعد يضم مخفف بإسكانها وهو جمع سعيد كرغيف ورغف

وإنما لم يصرفه الشاعر وإن كان مذكورا لأنه جعله اسما لأرض بعينها ويشبه

هذا قول الآخر:
# أحب الأيامي إذ بثينة أيم ... وأحببت لما ان عنيت الغواني
# الأيامي النسوة التي لا أزواج لهن والغواني المزوجات وقوله عنيت هو بكسر

التاء أي تزوجت وهذا الضرب من بديع الكلام أن يرجع من الغيبة إلى المخاطبة

فقال بثينة ثم قال عنيت وله نظائر كثيرة في القرآن العزيز منها قوله تعالى

(عبس وتولى أن جاءه الأعمى وما يدريك) وقوله (والحمد لله رب العالمين) إلى

قوله (إياك نعبد) وهو جاء عكسه وهو الرجوع من الخطاب إلى الغيبة فمن ذلك

قوله تعالى (حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم) . أخبرنا الأنباري عبد

الحافظ أخبرنا عبد القادر الرهاوي أخبرنا عبد الرحيم بن علي الشاهد أخبرنا

محمد بن طاهر المقدسي الحافظ أخبرنا أبو الفتح المفيد
# 
# أخبرنا أبو الحسن بن علي بن محمد بن طلحة حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد بن أيوب

الطبراني قال سمعت أبا يحيى زكريا بن يحيى الساجي رحمه الله  قال كنا نمشي

في أزقة البصرة إلى باب بعض المحدثين فأسرعت المشي وكان مع رجل منهم ماجن

في دينه فقال ارفعوا أرجلكم عن أجنحة الملائكة لا تكسروها كالمستهزئ فما

زال في موضعه حتى جفت رجلاه وسقط. وقال الحافظ عبد الحافظ إسناد هذه

الحكاية كالوجد أو كرأي العين لأن رواتها أعلام أئمة.
# وبالاسناد إلى المقدسي قال أخبرنا أبو الحسين يحيى بن الحسين العلوي

أخبرنا ابن الحسين الضبعي: قال سمعت عبد الله بن محمد بن محمد العكبري يقول

سمعت أبا عبد الله محمد بن يعقوب المتوثي يقول سمعت أبا داود السجستاني

يقول كان في أصحاب الحديث رجل خليع إلى أن سمع بحديث النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم أن الملائكة لتضع أجنحتها لطالب العلم رضا بما يصنع فجعل في عقبيه

مسامير حديد وقال أريد أن أطأ أجنحة الملائكة فأصابه أكلة في رجليه. قلت

المتوثي بميم مفتوحة ثم تاء مثناة من فوق مشددة مضمومة وواو ساكنة ثم ثاء

مثلثة ثم ياء النسب.
# وذكر الإمام أبو عبد الله محمد بن إسماعيل بن محمد بن الفضل التيمي رحمه

الله في كتابه شرح صحيح مسلم هذه الحكاية فيها وشلت رجلاه ويداه وسائر

أعضائه. قال وقرأت في بعض الحكايات أن بعض المبتدعة حين سمع قول النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم) إذا استيقظ أحدكم من نومه فلا يغمس يده في الإناء حتى

يغسلها فإنه لا يدري أين باتت يده (. قال ذلك المبتدع على سبيل التهكم أنا

أدري أين باتت يدي في الفراش فأصبح وقد أدخل يده في دبره إلى ذراعه. قال

التيمي فليتق المرء الاستحفاف بالسنن ومواضع التوقيف فانظر كيف وصل إليهما

شؤم فعلهما. قلت ومعنى هذا الحديث ما قاله الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى

عنه وغيره من العلماء رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن النائم تطوف يده في نومه على
# 
# بدنه فلا يأمن أنها مرت على نجاسة من دم بثرة أو قملة أو برغوث أو على

محل الاستنجاء وما أشبه ذلك والله أعلم.
# قوله شلت يداه أي يبست وبطلت  حركتها وهو بفتح الشين على اللغة الفصيحة

وفيها لغة أخرى بضمها والله أعلم. قلت ومن هذا المعنى ما وجد في زمامنا هذا

وتوارثت به الأخبار وثبتت عند القضاة أن رجلا بقرية ببلاد بصرى في أوائل

سنة خمس وستين وستمائة كان شاب سيئ الاعتقاد في أهل الخير وله ابن يعتقد

فيهم فجاء ابنه يوما من عند شيخ صالح ومعه مسواك فقال ما أعطاك شيخك؟

مستهزئا قال هذا المسواك فأخذه منه وأخله في دبره احتقارا له فبقي مدة ثم

ولد ذلك الرجل الذي أدخل المسواك في دبره جروا قريب الشبه بالسمكة فقتله ثم

مات الرجل في الحال أو بعد يومين عافانا الله الكريم من بلائه ووفقنا الله

لتنزيه السنن وتعظيم شعائره.
# أخبرنا الشيخ الفقيه المسدد أبو محمد عبد الرحمن بن سالم الأنباري رحمه

الله أخبرنا القاضي الإمام أبو القاسم عبد الصمد بن محمد بن أبي الفضل

الأنصاري أخبرنا الإمام أبو الفتح نصر الله بن محمد بن عبد القوي المصيصي

أخبرنا الشيخ الفقيه الإمام أبو الفتح نصر بن إبراهيم بن نصر المقدسي

الزاهد رضي الله تعالى عنه أخبرنا القاضي أبو الحسن محمد بن علي فيما كتب

إلي قال أخبرنا أحمد بن يعقوب الهروي قال حدثنا أبو عبد الله الروزبادي

حدثنا عمر بن مخلد الصوفي قال قال ابن أبي الورد قال معروف الكرخي رضي الله

تعالى عنه علامة مقت الله تعالى للعبد أن تراه مشتعلا بما لا يعنيه.
# أخبرنا شيخنا الحافظ أبو البقاء رحمه الله أخبرنا أبو محمد أخبرنا القاضي

أبو بكر أخبرنا الخطيب أخبرنا أبو سعيد يعني محمد بن موسى بن
# 
# الفضل بن إبراهيم قال سمعت الفضيل بن عياض رحمه الله تعالى يقول تسأله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ت-ر (satara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal, shield from sight; the act of veiling that which is shameful or defective.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, the divine attribute of concealment (sitr) parallels human obligation to veil a brother's sin, mirroring Allah's covering of His servant's faults.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical covering; metaphorical (majāz) — concealing a moral blemish, as in "he revived him," i.e., saved him from social death.
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥayya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To live, to be alive; revival (iḥyāʾ) as the restoration of life.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Life as the principle of sensation and action; metaphorically, preserving honor and dignity is a form of life-giving.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — biological life; metaphorical — the life of reputation and communal standing.
- Root: ع-ن-ي (ʿaniya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be concerned, to care; in the verse cited, ʿanītu (with kasrah on the tāʾ) means "I married" (tazawwajtu).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The shift from third-person to second-person (iltifāt) as a rhetorical device in the Qur'an, drawing the listener into direct address.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): This is the rhetorical figure of apostrophe (iltifāt), moving from ghaybah (absence) to khiṭāb (address), a hallmark of Qur'anic eloquence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Iltifāt (الالتفات) — The syntactic-rhetorical shift in person (from third to second, or vice versa) within a single discourse, permissible in Arabic for emphasis and emotional engagement, as exemplified in {«عبس وتولى»} and {«إياك نعبد»}.
chapters.translation:
I say: Whoever conceals (satara) the fault of his believing brother has, as it were, given him life (iḥyāʾ). Among the verses they recited concerning honoring one who holds a connection to the Beloved (i.e., the Prophet ﷺ) is the saying of one poet:

"Lo, I love the abodes for Saʿd's sake — indeed, I love the abodes for love of Fāṭimah."

Saʿd — with the ḍammah on the sīn (the unpointed letter) and sukūn on the ʿayn — is the name of a place in Nakhl. Abū Bakr al-Hamadhānī said in his book *Kitāb al-Ishtiqāq*: Its origin is Saʿd, pronounced with ḍammah, lightened by giving it sukūn, and it is a plural of Saʿīd, like *rughīf* and *rughf* (plurals of *raghīf*). The poet did not decline it (i.e., left it diptote), even though it is masculine, because he made it a proper name for a specific land. Similar to this is the saying of another:

"I loved the unmarried women when Buthaynah was unmarried, and I loved the married women when I myself married (ʿanītu)."

Al-Ayāmā refers to women who have no husbands, and al-Ghawānī refers to married women. His saying "ʿanītu" — with kasrah on the tāʾ — means "I married." This type of rhetorical excellence (badīʿ) is the turning from third-person narration (ghaybah) to direct address (khiṭāb): he said "Buthaynah" (in the third person), then said "ʿanītu" (in the first person). This has numerous parallels in the Mighty Qur'an, including His saying {«He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him — and what will make you know?»} (ʿAbasa 80:1-3), and His saying {«Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds»} up to His saying {«You alone we worship»} (al-Fātiḥah 1:2-5). The opposite also occurs — turning from direct address to third-person narration — as in His saying {«Until when you are in the ships and they sail with them»} (Yūnus 10:22).

Al-Anbārī ʿAbd al-Ḥāfiẓ informed us: ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Rahāwī informed us: ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn ʿAlī al-Shāhid informed us: Muḥammad ibn Ṭāhir al-Maqdisī al-Ḥāfiẓ informed us: Abū al-Fatḥ al-Mufīd informed us: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah informed us: Sulaymān ibn Aḥmad ibn Ayyūb al-Ṭabarānī related, saying: I heard Abū Yaḥyā Zakarīyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Sājī (may Allah have mercy on him) say: We were walking in the alleys of Baṣrah toward the door of one of the ḥadīth scholars, and I quickened my pace. With one of the men was a dissolute fellow (mājin) in his religion, who said — mockingly — "Lift your feet from the wings of the angels, lest you break them!" He (the mocker) remained in his place until his legs dried up and he fell. Al-Ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Ḥāfiẓ said: The chain of this anecdote is like a direct vision (ka-al-wajd) or like the eye's own sight, for its narrators are eminent imams.

By the same chain to al-Maqdisī, he said: Abū al-Ḥusayn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥusayn al-ʿAlawī informed us: Ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḍubʿī informed us, saying: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-ʿUkbarī say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Mutawwathī say: I heard Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī say: There was among the ḥadīth scholars a dissolute man (khalīʿ), until he heard the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "The angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he does." So he placed iron nails in his heels and said, "I want to tread upon the wings of the angels." Then a gangrene (aklah) afflicted his legs. I say: al-Mutawwathī — with a fatḥah on the mīm, then a shaddah on the tāʾ (the dotted letter above) with ḍammah, then a sukūn on the wāw, then a thāʾ (the three-dotted letter), then the yāʾ of attribution.

The Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Taymī (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned in his book *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* this anecdote, adding: "And his legs, hands, and all his limbs became paralyzed (shullat)." He said: And I read in some anecdotes that a certain innovator (mubtadiʿ), upon hearing the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "When one of you wakes from his sleep, let him not dip his hand into the vessel until he washes it, for he does not know where his hand spent the night" — that innovator said mockingly: "I know where my hand spent the night — in my bed!" And by morning, his hand had been inserted into his anus up to his forearm. Al-Taymī said: Let a man fear treating the Sunnahs lightly and the places of divine prohibition (tawqīf). See how the ill consequence of their deeds reached them both. I say: The meaning of this ḥadīth is what Imam al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) and other scholars (may Allah be pleased with them) said: The sleeper's hand wanders over his body during sleep, so one cannot be certain it has not passed over some impurity — blood from a pustule, a louse, a flea, or the place of istinjāʾ (cleansing after excretion) — or something similar. And Allah knows best.

His saying "shullat yadāhu" (his hands were paralyzed) means they became dry (yabisat) and their movement ceased. It is with fatḥah on the shīn in the eloquent language, and there is another dialect with ḍammah. And Allah knows best. I say: From this same meaning is what occurred in our own time, transmitted by reports and established before the judges: In a village in the lands of Baṣrā, at the beginning of the year 665 AH (1266 CE), there was a young man of evil belief concerning the people of goodness, and he had a son who held them in high regard. One day, the son came from a righteous shaykh with a toothstick (miswāk). The father said mockingly, "What did your shaykh give you?" He replied, "This toothstick." The father took it from him and inserted it into his own anus, despising it. He remained thus for a time, then that man who had inserted the toothstick into his anus gave birth to a puppy resembling a fish, and he killed it. Then the man died immediately, or after two days. May Allah the Generous protect us from His affliction, and may He grant us success in venerating the Sunnahs and magnifying His sacred rites.

The upright faqīh shaykh Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim al-Anbārī (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us: The judge and imam Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Faḍl al-Anṣārī informed us: The imam Abū al-Fatḥ Naṣr Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Qawī al-Miṣīṣī informed us: The faqīh and imam Abū al-Fatḥ Naṣr ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Naṣr al-Maqdisī al-Zāhid (may Allah be pleased with him) informed us: The judge Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed us in writing, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Harawī informed us, saying: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rūzabādī related to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Mukhallad al-Ṣūfī related to us, saying: Ibn Abī al-Ward said: Maʿrūf al-Karkhī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A sign of Allah's abandonment (maqt) of a servant is that you see him engrossed in what does not concern him.

Our shaykh, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Baqāʾ (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us: Abū Muḥammad informed us: The judge Abū Bakr informed us: Al-Khaṭīb informed us: Abū Saʿīd — meaning Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm — said: I heard al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) say: You ask him...

chapters.title_en: The Garden of the Gnostics — Section 14: On the Subtlety of Ostentation (Riyāʾ) and the Path of True Devotion
chapters.arabic_text:
الجنة وتأتي ما يكره ما رأيت أحدا أقل نظرا منك لنفسك.
# أخبرنا أبو البقاء حدثنا أبو محمد حدثنا أبو بكر الخطيب أخبرنا أبو

القاسم عبد الرحمن بن السراج قال سمعت أبا بكر أحمد بن السائح قال سمعت

القاسم بن محمد صاحب سهل يقول سمعت سهل بن عبد الله يقول  ليس بين العبد

وبين الله حجاب أغلظ من الدعوى ولا طريق إليه أقرب من الافتقار.
# وروينا بأسانيد صحيحة عن أبي يحيى النكراوي قال ما رأيت أعبد لله من شعبة

حتى جف جلده على عظمه ليس بينهما لحم وبلغنا عن الشافعي رحمه الله قال خير

الدنيا والآخرة في خمس خصال غنى النفس وكف الأذى وكسب الحلال ولباس التقوى

والثقة بالله عز وجل على كل حال.
# وعن الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى قال من غلبت عليه شدة الشهوة لحب الدنيا

لزمته العبودية لأهلها ومن رضي بالقنوع زال عنه الخضوع.
# 
# وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه من أحب أن يفتح الله قلبه ويرزقه العلم

فعليه بالخلوة وقلة الأكل وترك مخالطة السفهاء وبعض أهل العلم الذين ليس

معهم إنصاف ولا أدب. وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى أنفع الذخائر التقوى

وأضرها العدوان. وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه ورحمه أفضل الأعمال ثلاثة

ذكر الله تعالى ومواساة الأخوان وإنصاف الناس من نفسك: يعني هذه الثلاثة من

أفضل الأعمال. وقال الشافعي رحمه الله لا يعرف الرياء إلا مخلص. يعني لا

يتمكن في معرفة حقيقته والاطلاع على غوامض خفياته إلا من أراد الإخلاص فإنه

يجتهد أزمانا في مطاولة البحث والفكر والتنقيب عنده حتى يعرفه أو يعرف بعضه

ولا يحصل هذا لكل أحد وإنما يحصل هذا للخواص. وأما من يزعم من آحاد الناس

أنه يعرف الرياء فهو جهل منه بحقيقته.
# وسأذكر في هذا الكتاب بابا إن شاء الله تعالى ترى فيه من العجائب ما تقر

به عينك إن شاء الله تعالى، ويكفي في شدة خفائه ما رويناه عن الأستاذ

الإمام أبي القاسم القشيري رحمه الله في رسالته بإسنادنا المتقدم عنه قال

سمعت محمد بن الحسين يقول سمعت أحمد بن علي بن جعفر يقول سمعت الحسن بن

علوية يقول قال أبو يزيد رضي الله تعالى عنه كنت ثنتي عشرة سنة حداد نفسي

وخمس سنين كنت مرآة قلبي وسنة أنظر فيما بينهما فإذا في وسطي زنار ظاهر

فعملت في قطعه ثنتي عشرة  سنة ثم نظرت فإذا في باطني زنار فعملت في قطعه خمس

سنين أنظر كيف أقطع فكشف لي فنظرت إلى الخلق فرأيتهم موتى فكبرت عليهم أربع

تكبيرات.
# قلت يكفي في شدة خفاء الرياء اشتباهه هذا الاشتباه على هذا السيد الذي عز

نظيره في هذا الطريق وأما قوله فرأيتهم موتى فهو في غاية من النفاسة
# 
# والحسن قل إن يوجد في غير كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كلام يحصل معناه

وأنا أشير إلى معناه بعبارة وجيزة فمعناه أنه لما جاهد هذه المجاهدة وتهذيب

نفسه واستنار قلبه واستولى على نفسه وقهرها وملكها ملكا تاما وانقادت له

انقيادا خالصا نظر إلى جميع المخلوقين فوجدهم موتى لا حكم لهم فلا يضرون

وله ينفعون، ولا يعطون ولا يمنعون ولا يحيون ولا يميتون ولا يصلون ولا

يقطعون ولا يقربون ولا يبعدون ولا يسعدون ولا يشقون ولا يرزقون ولا يحرمون

ولا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا، وهذه

صفة الأموات أن يعاملوا معاملة الموتى في هذه الأمور المذكورة وأن لا

يخافوا ولا يرجوا ولا يطمع فيما عندهم ولا يراؤوا ولا يداهنوا ولا يشتغل

بهم ولا يحتقروا ولا ينتقصوا ولا تذكر عيوبهم ولا تتبع عثراتهم ولا ينقب عن

زلاتهم ولا يحسدوا ولا يستكثر فيهم ما أعطاهم الله تعالى من نعمة ويرحموا

ويعذروا فيما يأتونه من النقائص مع أنا نقيم الحدود عليهم ما جاء الشرع به

من الحدود ولا يمنعنا إقامة الحد ما قدمناه ولا يمنعنا أيضا ما قدمناه من

إقامة الحد أنا نحرص على ستر عوراتهم من غير تنقص لهم بها يفعل ذلك بالميت

وإذا ذكرهم ذاكر بشين نهيناه عن الخوض في ذلك كما ننهاه عن ذلك في الميت

ولا نفعل شيئا لهم ولا نتركه ولا نمتنع من القيام بشيء من طاعات الله

بسببهم ولا نمتنع من ذلك بسبب الميت ولا نتكثر بمدحهم.
# ولا نحبه ولا نكره سبهم إيانا ولا نقابله فالحاصل أنهم كالعدم في جميع ما

ذكرناه فهم مدبرون تجري فيهم أحكام  الله تعالى فمن عاملهم هذه المعاملة جمع

خير الآخرة والدنيا نسأل الله الكريم التوفيق لذلك. فهذه الأحرف كافية في

الاشارة إلى شرح كلامه رضي الله عنه والله أعلم.
# وروينا بإسنادنا إلى القشيري رحمه الله قال سمعت الشيخ أبا عبد الرحمن

يعني السلمي إما الصوفية في زمانه وبعده قال سمعت العباس البغدادي يقول

سمعت جعفرا يقول سمعت الجنيد يقول سمعت السري رحمه الله يقول يا معشر

الشباب جدوا قبل أن تبلغوا مبلغي فتضعفوا وتقصروا كما قصرت قال وكان في ذلك

الوقت لا تلحقه الشباب إلى العبادة. وقال
# 
# أحمد بن أبي الحواري في كتاب الزهد حدثنا سويد قال رأيت إبن أبي مرئد في

السوق وفي يده عرق ورغيف وهو يأكل وكان طلب للقضاء ففعل ذلك حتى تخلص قلت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, claim, or assert; the act of laying claim to something (daʿwā) — a pretension of station or right.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, daʿwā denotes the soul's false claim to self-sufficiency or rank before God — the antithesis of servitude (ʿubūdiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a legal claim or summons. Metaphorical: the ego's pretentious assertion of worth, which veils the servant from God.
- Root: ف-ق-ر (fa-qa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Poverty, neediness; a gap or hollow — the state of being devoid.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ontological poverty before God (iftiqār) — the creature's absolute need for the Necessary Existent; the highest station of servitude.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: material destitution. Metaphorical: the soul's recognition of its utter dependence on God, the closest path to Him.
- Root: ر-ي-ء (rā-yā-hamza)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To see, to show; riyāʾ — ostentation, performing acts to be seen by others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The hidden disease of the heart that corrupts sincerity (ikhlāṣ); its subtlety is such that only the truly sincere can perceive its reality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: visual perception. Metaphorical: the inward display of piety for creatures, a veil thicker than any physical barrier.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — In the phrase "ليس بين العبد وبين الله حجاب أغلظ من الدعوى" the elative "أغلظ" functions as a predicate requiring a circumstantial accusative understood, governing the comparative sense of absolute exclusion (no veil is thicker than...), demanding the reader grasp the syntactic ellipsis of "min" as a particle of comparison initiating a full clause of exception.
chapters.translation:
I say: Paradise comes, and what it dislikes — I have never seen anyone with less regard for his own soul than you.

# We were informed by Abū al-Baqāʾ, who reported from Abū Muḥammad, who reported from Abū Bakr al-Khaṭīb, who reported from Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Sarrāj, who said: I heard Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Sāʾiḥ say: I heard al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, the companion of Sahl, say: I heard Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: There is no veil thicker between the servant and God than pretension (al-daʿwā), and no path to Him nearer than neediness (al-iftiqār).

# And we have related through sound chains of transmission (asānīd ṣaḥīḥah) from Abū Yaḥyā al-Nakrāwī, who said: I never saw anyone more devoted in worship to God than Shuʿbah — until his skin dried upon his bone, with no flesh between them. And it has reached us from al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, that he said: The good of this world and the Hereafter lies in five qualities: richness of the soul (ghinā al-nafs), refraining from harm (kaf al-adhā), earning what is lawful (kasb al-ḥalāl), the garment of piety (libās al-taqwā), and trust in God, Mighty and Majestic, in every circumstance.

# And from al-Shāfiʿī, may God Most High have mercy on him, he said: Whoever is overcome by the intensity of lust for love of this world, servitude to its people becomes incumbent upon him; and whoever is content with sufficiency (al-qunūʿ), abasement departs from him.

# And al-Shāfiʿī, may God Most High be pleased with him, said: Whoever loves that God open his heart and grant him knowledge — let him adhere to seclusion (al-khalwah), eating little, and abandoning the company of fools and of those scholars who possess neither fairness (inṣāf) nor discipline (adab). And al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said: The most beneficial of treasures is piety (al-taqwā), and the most harmful is transgression (al-ʿudwān). And al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him and have mercy on him, said: The most excellent of deeds are three: the remembrance of God Most High, consoling the brethren (muwāsāt al-ikhwān), and treating people fairly from oneself (inṣāf al-nās min nafsik) — meaning: these three are among the most excellent of deeds. And al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, said: None knows ostentation (al-riyāʾ) except the sincere one (mukhliṣ) — meaning: none is able to know its reality and perceive its hidden subtleties except one who intends sincerity (ikhlāṣ), for he strives for long periods in prolonged search, reflection, and investigation until he knows it, or knows part of it. And this is not attained by everyone; rather, it is attained only by the elite (al-khawāṣṣ). As for one who claims from among the common people that he knows ostentation — that is ignorance on his part of its reality.

# And I shall mention in this book a chapter, God willing, in which you will see wonders that will delight your eye, God willing. And it suffices for the intensity of its hiddenness what we have related from the master Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, may God have mercy on him, in his Epistle (Risālah), through our aforementioned chain from him. He said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn say: I heard Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar say: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlawiyyah say: Abū Yazīd, may God be pleased with him, said: For twelve years I was the blacksmith of my soul (ḥaddād nafsī), and for five years I was the mirror of my heart (mirʾāt qalbī), and for a year I looked between the two — and behold, around my waist was a visible girdle (zunnār). So I labored in cutting it for twelve years. Then I looked, and behold, in my inward was a girdle. So I labored in cutting it for five years, contemplating how to cut it. Then it was unveiled to me, and I looked at creation and saw them dead — so I pronounced over them four takbīrs (funeral cries).

I say: It suffices for the intensity of the hiddenness of ostentation that it was confused with this very confusion upon this master whose like is rare in this path. As for his saying, "I saw them dead" — it is at the utmost degree of preciousness.

# And the good — rarely is found outside the speech of the Prophet, peace be upon him, speech that achieves its meaning. And I shall point to its meaning with a concise expression. Its meaning is: When he struggled this struggle (mujāhadah) and refined his soul, and his heart was illumined, and he gained mastery over his soul, subdued it, and possessed it with complete possession, and it yielded to him with pure obedience — he looked at all creatures and found them dead, having no authority. They neither harm nor benefit; they neither give nor withhold; they neither give life nor cause death; they neither connect nor sever; they neither bring near nor distance; they neither make fortunate nor wretched; they neither provide sustenance nor deprive; they own not for themselves benefit nor harm, and they own not death, nor life, nor resurrection. And this is the description of the dead — that they be treated as the dead are treated in these aforementioned matters: that they be neither feared nor hoped in, nor that one covet what they possess, nor that one show off before them, nor flatter them, nor occupy oneself with them, nor despise them, nor belittle them, nor mention their faults, nor pursue their slips, nor dig into their missteps, nor envy them, nor deem much what God Most High has given them of blessing — but rather that one have mercy on them and excuse them for the deficiencies they commit. Yet we establish the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) upon them as the Sacred Law has brought of punishments; and our establishing the punishment does not prevent what we have mentioned, nor does what we have mentioned prevent our establishing the punishment — that we are eager to conceal their faults without belittling them thereby, just as one does with the dead. And if a mentioner mentions them with something shameful, we forbid him from delving into that, just as we forbid him from that regarding the dead. And we do not do anything for them nor leave it, and we do not refrain from performing any of the acts of obedience to God because of them, nor do we refrain from that because of the dead. And we do not seek increase by praising them.

# Nor do we love their praise of us, nor hate their reviling of us, nor do we retaliate against it. The sum is: they are as non-existent (al-ʿadam) in all that we have mentioned — for they are governed, and the judgments of God Most High run upon them. So whoever treats them with this treatment gathers the good of the Hereafter and this world. We ask God the Generous for success in that. These letters suffice as an indication toward the explanation of his speech, may God be pleased with him. And God knows best.

# And we have related through our chain to al-Qushayrī, may God have mercy on him, who said: I heard the Shaykh Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — meaning al-Sulamī, the imām of the Sufis in his time and after him — say: I heard al-ʿAbbās al-Baghdādī say: I heard Jaʿfar say: I heard al-Junayd say: I heard al-Sarī, may God have mercy on him, say: O company of youth! Strive earnestly before you reach my station, lest you become weak and fall short as I fell short. He said: And at that time, youth could not overtake him in worship. And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said in the Book of Asceticism (Kitāb al-Zuhd): Suwayd related to us, saying: I saw Ibn Abī Murrad in the market, and in his hand was a sinew and a loaf, and he was eating — and he had sought the judgeship, so he did this until he was freed. I say: [This suffices].

chapters.title_en: On Refinement of Conduct, Consolation, and the Miracles of the Saints (Karāmāt al-Awliyā')
chapters.arabic_text:
العرق بفتح العين وإسكان الراء هو العظم عليه قليل لحم ومما يشبه هذا ما

رواه الإمام البيهقي بإسناد عن الإمام الشافعي رحمه الله قال دخل سفيان

الثوري رضي الله تعالى عنه على أمير المؤمنين فجعل يتجانن عليهم ويمسح

البساط ويقول ما أحسنه بكم أخذتم هذا قال البول البول حتى أخرج يعني حتى

أخرج يريد أنه احتال ليتباعد عنهم. ويسم من أمرهم قال الشافعي رضي الله

تعالى عنه مات ابن للحسين بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما فلم ير عليه كآبة

فعوتب في ذلك فقال أنا أهل بيت نسأل الله تعالى فيعطينا فإذا أراد ما نكره

فيما يجب رضينا. وقال أحمد بن أبي الحواري سمعت أبا سليمان يقول ما نحب من

نحب إلا بطاعتهم لمؤدبهم وأنت تعصيني قد أمرتك أن تفتح أصابعك. وفي الترمذي

ضمها. وعن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه نظر إلى ابنه فاقل إني

لأعلم خلة فيك قال وما هي قال تموت فاحتسبه. وعن أبي الحسن المدائني قال

قيل لأعرابية ما أحسن عزاك على ابنك فقالت أن فقد أبيه أنسى المصائب بعده.

وقال موسى بن المهتدي
# 
# لإبراهيم بن سلم وعزاه بابنه فقال أسرك وهو بلية وفتنة وحزنك وهو صلوات

ورحمة.  قال وكتب رجل إلى بعض إخوانه يعزيه بإبنه أما بعد فإن الولد على

والده ما عاش حزن وفتنة وإذا قدمه فصلاة ورحمة فلا تجزع على ما فاتك من

حزنه وفتنته ولا تضيع ما عوضك الله تعالى من صلاته ورحمته. وقال أحمد بن

أبي الحواري سمعت أبا سليمان يقول أقمت عشرين سنة لم أحتلم فأحدثت بمكة

حدثا فما أصبحت حتى احتلمت فقلت وأي شيء كان الحدث قال تركت صلاة العشاء

الآخرة في المسجد الحرام في جماعة.
# وروينا عن الإمام مالك رضي الله عنه تلقى الرجل وما يلحن حرفا وعمله لحن

كله.
# وروينا عن الإمام أبي بكر محمد بن يحيى بن عبد الله بن العباس بن محمد بن

صول المصولي بضم الصاد المهملة وإسكان الواو قال بعض الزهاد أعربنا في

كلامنا فما نلحن ولحنا في أعمالنا فما نعرب قال الشاعر:
# لم نؤت من جهل ولكننا ... نستر وجه العلم بالجهل
# نكره أن نلحن في قولنا ... وما نبالي اللحن في الفعل
# وأخبرنا الشيخ أبو محمد اسماعيل بن أبي إسحاق إبراهيم بن أبي البشر شاكر

أخبرنا أبو طاهر بركات بن إبراهيم بن طاهر الخشوعي أخبرنا أبو محمد هبة

الله بن أحمد بن محمد الاكفاني حدثنا أبو بكر أحمد بن علي بن ثابت البغدادي

الحافظ أخبرنا عبيد الله بن عمر الواعظ حدثني عبد الله بن محمد بن نصر بن

علي الجهضمي حدثني محمد بن خالد حدثنا علي بن نصر قال رأيت الخليل بن أحمد

رحمة الله في النوم فقلت في منامي لا أرى أحدا أعقل من الخليل فقلت ما صنع

الله بك قال رأيت ما كنا فيه فإنه لم يكن شيء أفضل من سبحان الله والحمد

لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر. وفي رواية قال علي بن نصر رأيت الخليل بن

أحمد في المنام فقلت له ما فعل ربك بك قال غفر لي قلت بم نجوت قال بلا حول

ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم. قلت كيف وجدت علمك أعني العروض والأدب

والشعر قال وجدته  هباء منثورا.
# 
# وبهذا الاسناد إلى أحمد بن علي بن ثابت قال أنشدنا أبو الحسن محمد بن

المظفر أنشدنا أبو بكر أحمد بن سليمان النجار أنشدنا هلال بن العلاء لنفسه:
# سيبلى لسان كان يعرف لفظه ... فيا ليته في وقفة العرض يسلم
# وما ينفع الاعراب إن لم يكن تقي ... وما ضر ذا التقوى لسان معجم
#

| باب في كرامات الأولياء ومواهبهم
# قال الله تعالى: (ألا إن أولياء الله خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون. الذين

آمنوا وكانوا يتقون. لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل

لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم) .
# اعلم أن مذهب أهل الحق إثبات كرامات الأولياء وأنها واقعة موجودة مستمرة

في الأعصار ويدل عليه دلائل العقول وصرائح النقول. أما دلائل العقل فهي أمر

يمكن حدوثه ولا يؤدي وقوعه إلى رفع أصل من أصول الدين فيجب وصف الله تعالى

بالقدرة عليه وما كان مقدورا كان جائز الوقوع. وأما النقول فآيات في القرآن

العظيم وأحاديث مستفيضة. أما الآيات فقوله تعالى النقول فآيات في القرآن

العظيم وأحاديث مستفيضة. أما الآيات فقوله تعالى في قصة مريم.
# (وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا) .
# قال الإمام أبو المعالي رحمه الله تعالى إمام الحرمين ولم تكن مريم بنبية

باجماع العلماء وكذا قاله غيره بل كانت ولية صديقة كما أخبر الله تعالى

عنها.
# وقوله تعالى: (كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب، وجد عندها رزقا، قال يا

مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله) .
# 
# ومن ذلك قصة صاحب سليمان عليه السلام حيث قال: (أنا آتيك به قبل أن يرتد

إليك طرفك) .
# قال العلماء ولم يكن نبيا. ومن ذلك ما استدل به إمام الحرمين وغيره من

قصة أم موسى. ومن ذلك ما استدل به أبو القاسم القشيري من قصة ذي القرنين.

واستدل القشيري وغيره بقصة الخضر مع موسى عليه السلام قالوا ولم يكن نبيا

بل وليا وهذا خلاف المختار والذي عليه الأكثرون أنه كان نبيا. وقبل كان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ق (ʿ-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A bone with little flesh upon it; also sweat, or a vein from which blood flows.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used metaphorically for that which is meager or of scant substance—here, the worldly life's fleeting nature.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: bone with scant meat; metaphorical: a paltry thing, evoking the insignificance of worldly trials.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "يعني حتى أخرج" (meaning: until he left) functions as an explicative gloss, clarifying the intent of the preceding verb "أخرج" (he went out), a common device in narrative transmission.
chapters.translation:
I say: The word "ʿaraq" (with fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the rā') is the bone upon which there is little flesh. And resembling this [i.e., the notion of scant worldly substance] is what was narrated by Imam al-Bayhaqī with his chain of transmission from Imam al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: Sufyān al-Thawrī, may Allah be pleased with him, entered upon the Commander of the Faithful [al-Mahdī], and he began to feign madness before them, wiping the carpet and saying, "How excellent this is for you! You have taken this." Then he said, "Urine! Urine!" until he was brought out—meaning, until he left—intending thereby to contrive a means of distancing himself from them and their affair. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: A son of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, died, and no gloom was seen upon him. He was reproached for that, and he said: "We are a household who ask Allah, and He gives us. So when He wills what we dislike in that which necessitates our contentment, we are pleased." And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: I heard Abū Sulaymān say: "We love none whom we love except through their obedience to their discipliner. And you disobey me—I have commanded you to open your fingers." And in al-Tirmidhī: "to close them." And from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, that he looked at his son and said: "Indeed, I know a trait in you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "You will die, so reckon it [as a reward]." And from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī, he said: It was said to a Bedouin woman: "How excellent is your consolation for your son!" She said: "His father's loss made me forget the calamities after him." And Mūsā ibn al-Muhtadī said to Ibrāhīm ibn Salam, consoling him for his son: "Your joy in him—while he is a trial and a tribulation—and your grief for him—while he is prayers and mercy." He said: And a man wrote to one of his brothers, consoling him for his son: "To proceed: verily, a son is for his father, as long as he lives, a grief and a tribulation; and when he precedes him [in death], then he is prayers and mercy. So do not be distressed over what has passed of your grief and tribulation, and do not squander what Allah has compensated you with of his prayers and mercy." And Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: I heard Abū Sulaymān say: "I remained twenty years without having a nocturnal emission. Then I committed an offense in Mecca, and I had not reached morning until I had one." I said: "And what was the offense?" He said: "I abandoned the final night prayer in the Sacred Mosque in congregation." And we have narrated from Imam Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him: "A man may be received [with honor] and not err in a single letter [of speech], while his deeds are all error." And we have narrated from Imam Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṣūl al-Mawṣūlī (with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the wāw), that one of the ascetics said: "We have become precise in our speech, so we do not err grammatically, but we err in our deeds, so we do not become precise." The poet said:
"We were not afflicted from ignorance, but we ... conceal the face of knowledge with ignorance.
We dislike erring in our speech ... yet we care not about erring in action."
And our shaykh Abū Muḥammad Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bashar Shākir informed us: Abū Ṭāhir Barakāt ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭāhir al-Khushūʿī informed us: Abū Muḥammad Hibat Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Akfānī informed us: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Thābit al-Baghdādī al-Ḥāfiẓ narrated to us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Wāʿiẓ informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī narrated to me: Muḥammad ibn Khālid narrated to me: ʿAlī ibn Naṣr narrated to us, saying: I saw al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him, in a dream. I said in my sleep: "I see none more intelligent than al-Khalīl." Then I said: "What has Allah done with you?" He said: "I saw what we were in—for there was nothing better than 'Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greatest.'" And in another narration, ʿAlī ibn Naṣr said: I saw al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad in a dream and said to him: "What has your Lord done with you?" He said: "He has forgiven me." I said: "By what did you attain salvation?" He said: "By 'There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent.'" I said: "How did you find your knowledge—I mean prosody, literature, and poetry?" He said: "I found it as scattered dust." And by this chain to Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Thābit, he said: Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Muẓaffar recited to us: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Sulaymān al-Najjār recited to us: Hilāl ibn al-ʿAlāʾ recited to us, for himself:
"A tongue that once knew its expression will perish ... would that it were safe at the standing for judgment.
And what avails grammatical precision if one is not pious ... and what harms the possessor of piety a barbarous tongue?"

| Chapter on the Miracles of the Saints and Their Divine Gifts

Allah the Exalted said: {«ألا إن أولياء الله خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون. الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون. لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم»} ("Verily, the friends of Allah—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve. Those who believed and were righteous. For them is glad tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah. That is the great attainment.")

Know that the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) is the affirmation of the miracles of the saints (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ), and that they are real, existent, and continuous across the ages. This is evidenced by the proofs of the intellect and the explicit texts of revelation. As for the proofs of the intellect: it is a matter whose occurrence is possible, and its actualization does not entail the nullification of any foundational principle of religion. Thus, it is obligatory to describe Allah the Exalted as having power over it, and whatever is within His power is permissible of occurrence. As for the textual proofs: they are verses in the Mighty Quran and widely transmitted hadiths. As for the verses: His saying, the Exalted, in the story of Mary: {«وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا»} ("And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe fresh dates.") Imam Abū al-Maʿālī, may Allah have mercy on him—the Imam of the Two Sanctuaries—said: Mary was not a prophetess by the consensus of the scholars, and others besides him said the same. Rather, she was a saintly, veracious woman (waliyya ṣiddīqa), as Allah the Exalted informed about her. And His saying, the Exalted: {«كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب، وجد عندها رزقا، قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله»} ("Whenever Zachariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said: 'O Mary, from where is this for you?' She said: 'It is from Allah.'") And from that is the story of the companion of Solomon, peace be upon him, where he said: {«أنا آتيك به قبل أن يرتد إليك طرفك»} ("I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.") The scholars said: He was not a prophet. And from that is what the Imam of the Two Sanctuaries and others adduced from the story of the mother of Moses. And from that is what Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī adduced from the story of Dhū al-Qarnayn. And al-Qushayrī and others adduced the story of al-Khiḍr with Moses, peace be upon him. They said: He was not a prophet, but rather a saint. And this contradicts the chosen view, and the view of the majority is that he was a prophet. And before [this chapter], it has [already] been [discussed].

chapters.title_en: On the Miracles of Saints (Karāmāt al-Awliyā') and Their Distinction from Prophetic Miracles (Muʿjizāt)
chapters.arabic_text:
نبيا رسولا وقيل كان وليا وقيل ملكا. وقد أوضحت  الخلاف فيه وشرحته في تهذيب

الأسماء واللغات وفي شرح المهذب. وفي ذلك قصة أهل الكهف وما اشتملت عليه من

خوارق العادات. قال إمام الحرمين وغيره ولم يكونوا أنبياء بالإجماع.
# وأما الأحاديث فكثيرة منها حديث أنس أن رجلين من أصحاب النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم خرجا من عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ليلة مظلمة ومعهما مثل

المصباحين يضيئان بين أيديهما فلما افترقا صار مع كل واحد منهما واحدا حتى

أتى أهله. أخرجه
# 
# البخاري في صحيحه في كتاب الصلاة وفي علامات النبوة هذان الرجلان عباد بن

البشر وأسيد بن حضير بضم أولهما وفتح ثانيهما. وحضير بضم الحاء المهملة

وبالضاد المعجمة. ومنها حديث أصحاب الغار الثلاثة الذين أووا إلى الغار

فأطبقت صخرة عليهم بابه فدعا كل واحد منهم بدعوة فانفرجت عنهم الصخرة وهو

مخرج في صحيحي البخاري ومسلم. ومنها حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه في

قصة جريج أنه قال للصبي الرضيع من أبوك قال فلان الراعي وهو مخرج في

الصحيح. ومنها حديث أبي هريرة قال:) قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لقد كان

فيما قبلكم من الأمم محدثون فإن يكن في أمتي أحد فإنه عمر (وفي رواية) قد

كان فيمن قبلكم من بني إسرائيل يكلمون من غير أن يكونوا أنبياء (رواه

البخاري في صحيحه. ومنها الحديث المشهور في صحيح البخاري وغيره في قصة حبيب

الأنصاري بضم الخاء المعجمة رضي الله تعالى عنه صاحب رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم. وقول ابنة الحارث فيه والله ما رأيت أسيرا قط خيرا من خبيب

والله لقد وجدته يوما يأكل من قطف عنب في يده وأنه لموثق في الحديد وما

بمكة من ثمر وكانت تقول أنه لرزق الله رزقه خبيبا. والأحاديث والآثار

وأقوال السلف والخلف في هذا الباب أكثر من أن تحصر فيكتفي بما أشرنا إليه

وسترى في هذا الباب جملا من ذلك وباقي الكتاب إن شاء الله تعالى.
# قال الإمام أبو المعالي إمام الحرمين الذي صار إليه أهل الحق جوار انخراق

العادة  في حق الأولياء وأطبقت المعتزلة على إنكار ذلك ثم من أهل الحق من

صار إلى أن الكرامة الخارقة للعادة شرطها أن تجري من غير إيثار واختيار من

الولي وصار هؤلاء إلى أن الكرامة تفارق المعجزة من هذا الوجه. قال الإمام

وهذا القول غير صحيح. وصار آخرون منهم إلى تجويز وقوع الكرامة على حكم

الاختيار ولكنهم منعوا وقوعها على مقتضى الدعوى فقالوا إذا ادعى الولي

الولاية واعتضد في إثبات دعواه بما يخرق العادة فكان ذلك ممتنعا. وهؤلاء

فرقوا بين الكرامة المعجزة بهذا قال وهذه الطريقة غير مرضية أيضا قال ولا

يمتنع عندنا ظهور خوارق العوائد مع الدعوى المفروضة. قال
# 
# وصار بعض أصحابنا إلى أن ما وقع معجزة النبي لا يجوز تقدير وقوعه كرامة

لولي فيمتنع عند هؤلاء أن ينفلق البحر وينقلب العصا ثعبانا ويحيى الموتى

إلى غير ذلك من آيات الأنبياء كرامة لولي. قال الإمام وهذه الطريقة غير

سديدة أيضا قال والمرضى عندنا جواز خوارق العادات في معارض الكرامات الفرق

بين المعجزة والكرامة فلا يفترقان في جواز العقل إلا بوقوع المعجزة على حسب

دعوى النبوة ووقع دون ادعاء النبوة. قال الإمام وقد جرى من الآيات في مولد

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما لا ينكره منتم إلى الإسلام وذلك قبل

النبوة والانبعاث. والمعجزة لا تسبق دعوى النبوة فكان كرامة قال فإن زعم

متعسف أن الآيات التي استدللنا بها كانت معجزات لنبي كل عصر فذلك اقتحام

منه للجهالات فإنا إذا بحثنا عن الأعصار الخالية لم نجد الآيات التي تمسكنا

بها مقترنة بدعوى نبوة ولا وقعت عن تحدي متحد فإن قالوا وقعت للأنبياء دون

عوامهم قلنا شرط المعجزة الدعوى فإذا فقدت كانت خارقة للعادة كرامة

للأنبياء ونجعل ذلك غرضنا إلى إثبات الكرامات. ولم يكن وقت مولد نبينا محمد

صلى الله وسلم نبي تستند آياته. قال الإمام فقد وضحت الكرامات جوازا ووقوعا

سمعا وعقلا. قال الامام وغيره في الفرق بين السحر والكرامة أن السحر لا

يظهر إلا على فاسق قال وليس ذلك من  مقتضيات العقل ولكنه ملقى من إجماع

الأمة. قال الامام ثم الكرامة وإن كانت لا تظهر على فاسق معلن بفسقه فلا

تشهد بالولاية على القطع إذ لو شهدت بها لأمن صواحبها العواقب وذلك لم يجز

لولي في كرامة باتفاق. هذا آخر كلام إمام الحرمين.
# قال الامام الاستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري رحمه الله فيما رويناه في رسالته

ظهور الكرامات علامة صدق من ظهرت عليه في أحواله فمن لم يكن صادقا فظهور

مثله عليه لا يجوز قال ولا بد من أن تكون الكرامة فعلا ناقضا للعادة في

أيام التكليف ظاهرا على موصوف بالولاية في معنى تصديقه في حاله قال وتكلم

أهل الحق في الفرق بين الكرامة والمعجزة فكان الإمام أبو إسحاق الاسفرايني

رحمه الله يقول المعجزات دلالات صدق الأنبياء ودليل النبوة لا
# 
# يوجد مع غير النبي. وكان يقول الأولياء لهم كرامات منها إجابة سنة الدعاء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ر-م (k-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Generosity, nobility, honor; a karāmah is an act of divine generosity bestowed upon a friend of God (walī).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, karāmah denotes a supernatural event (khāriq al-ʿādah) granted by God to a righteous non-prophet as honor and confirmation, distinct from muʿjizah which validates prophetic claims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "noble gift"; metaphorically extended to divine favors that breach customary natural laws, emphasizing God's sovereign bestowal rather than the saint's agency.
- Root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tear, rend, pierce; khāriq al-ʿādah is that which "tears through" the fabric of habitual natural causation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for supernatural occurrences—events that rupture the established order (ʿādah) of creation, used across discussions of prophethood and sainthood.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal tearing of cloth; metaphorical for breaking normative patterns, signaling divine intervention beyond secondary causality.
- Root: م-ع-ج-ز (m-ʿ-j-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: From ʿajaza (to be incapable); muʿjizah is that which renders others incapable of replicating—a miraculous proof.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The prophetic miracle is specifically tied to a claim (daʿwā) of prophethood and a challenge (taḥaddī); it authenticates the messenger's truthfulness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "incapacitating act"; rhetorically, it is a sign that silences opponents by exceeding human capacity, always conjoined with prophetic assertion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnā') — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if a saint claims sainthood...") and exceptive particles (illā) to delineate the precise boundaries between karāmah and muʿjizah, requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: And it was said [concerning al-Khiḍr] that he was a prophet and a messenger, and it was said he was a saint (walī), and it was said he was an angel. I have already clarified the disagreement concerning him and expounded it in Tahdhīb al-Asmā' wa al-Lughāt and in Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab. And in that [connection] is the story of the People of the Cave (Aṣḥāb al-Kahf) and what it comprises of supernatural occurrences (khawāriq al-ʿādāt). The Imām al-Ḥaramayn and others said: "They were not prophets by consensus."

As for the hadiths [on this topic], they are numerous. Among them is the hadith of Anas that two men from the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) departed from the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on a dark night, and with them were something like two lamps illuminating before them. When they separated, one [light] went with each of them until each reached his family. Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Ṣaḥīḥ in the Book of Prayer and in [the chapter on] Signs of Prophethood. These two men were ʿAbbād ibn Bishr and Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr—the first [letter of Usayd] is with ḍammah and the second with fatḥah; and Ḥuḍayr is with ḍammah on the unpointed ḥā' and with the pointed ḍād.

Among them is the hadith of the three [men of] the cave who sought refuge in a cave, and a rock sealed its entrance upon them. Each of them supplicated with a prayer, and the rock opened for them. It is transmitted in both Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

Among them is the hadith of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him) concerning the story of Jurayj, that he said to the suckling infant: "Who is your father?" He said: "So-and-so, the shepherd." It is transmitted in the Ṣaḥīḥ.

Among them is the hadith of Abū Hurayrah who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«لَقَدْ كَانَ فِيمَا قَبْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأُمَمِ مُحَدَّثُونَ فَإِنْ يَكُنْ فِي أُمَّتِي أَحَدٌ فَإِنَّهُ عُمَرُ»} ("Indeed, there were among the nations before you those who were inspired [muḥaddathūn]; if there is one among my nation, it is ʿUmar.") And in another narration: {«قَدْ كَانَ فِيمَنْ قَبْلَكُمْ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ يُكَلَّمُونَ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكُونُوا أَنْبِيَاءَ»} ("There were among those before you of the Children of Israel those who were spoken to without being prophets.") Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

Among them is the well-known hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and others concerning the story of Ḥabīb al-Anṣārī—with ḍammah on the pointed khā' (may God be pleased with him), the companion of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)—and the statement of the daughter of al-Ḥārith concerning him: "By God, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By God, I found him one day eating from a cluster of grapes in his hand while he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit in Mecca." She used to say: "It was provision (rizq) that God provided to Khubayb."

The hadiths, reports (āthār), and sayings of the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf) on this topic are too numerous to be encompassed. What we have indicated suffices, and you will see in this section a portion of that, and in the rest of the book, God willing.

The Imām Abū al-Maʿālī, Imām al-Ḥaramayn—to whom the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) turned—said: The occurrence of supernatural events (khawāriq al-ʿādah) in favor of saints (awliyā') is permissible [by consensus of the orthodox]. The Muʿtazilah unanimously denied that. Then among the people of truth, some held that the condition of a miracle of sanctity (karāmah) that breaches custom is that it occur without the saint's intention or choice (īthār wa ikhtiyār). These held that the karāmah differs from the prophetic miracle (muʿjizah) in this respect. The Imām said: "This statement is not sound."

Others among them held the permissibility of the karāmah occurring according to choice, but they prevented its occurrence in accordance with a claim [of sainthood]. They said: "If a saint claims sainthood and supports his claim with what breaches custom, that is impossible." These distinguished between the karāmah and the muʿjizah by this [criterion]. He said: "This method is also not satisfactory."

He said: "It is not impossible in our view that supernatural events occur alongside the aforementioned claim." He said: "Some of our companions held that what occurs as a miracle of a prophet cannot be estimated to occur as a karāmah for a saint. Thus, in their view, it is impossible for the sea to split, the staff to turn into a serpent, the dead to be revived, and other such signs of the prophets to occur as a karāmah for a saint." The Imām said: "This method is also not sound."

He said: "What is approved in our view is the permissibility of supernatural events in general. The difference between the muʿjizah and the karāmah is that they do not differ in rational permissibility except that the muʿjizah occurs in accordance with the claim of prophethood, while the karāmah occurs without a claim of prophethood."

The Imām said: "There occurred of the signs (āyāt) at the birth of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) what no one affiliated with Islam denies—and that was before prophethood and his being sent. The muʿjizah does not precede the claim of prophethood, so that was a karāmah."

He said: "If a perverse person claims that the signs we have adduced were miracles of a prophet of every era, that is his plunging into ignorances. For when we investigate past eras, we do not find the signs to which we cling conjoined with a claim of prophethood, nor did they occur upon a challenge (taḥaddī) from any challenger."

If they say: "They occurred for prophets, not for their common folk," we say: "The condition of the muʿjizah is the claim [of prophethood]. When that is absent, the supernatural event is a karāmah for the prophets [themselves]—and we make that our aim in establishing the karāmāt. And there was no prophet at the time of the birth of our Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) to whom his signs could be attributed."

The Imām said: "Thus the karāmāt have been clarified in permissibility and occurrence, by transmission (samʿan) and by reason (ʿaqlan)."

The Imām and others said concerning the difference between sorcery (siḥr) and the karāmah: "Sorcery does not appear except upon a wicked person (fāsiq)." He said: "That is not a requirement of reason, but it is received from the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the community."

The Imām said: "Then the karāmah, even though it does not appear upon a person openly wicked in his wickedness, does not testify to sainthood with certainty (qaṭʿ). For if it so testified, its possessor would be secure from [evil] consequences—and that is not permissible for a saint in a karāmah by agreement." This is the end of the speech of Imām al-Ḥaramayn.

The Imām, the master (ustādh), Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī (may God have mercy on him) said, in what we have narrated in his Risālah: "The appearance of karāmāt is a sign of the truthfulness of the one upon whom they appear in his states. Whoever is not truthful, the appearance of such upon him is not permissible." He said: "It is necessary that the karāmah be an act that breaks custom (nāqiḍ li al-ʿādah) during the days of obligation (taklīf), appearing upon one described with sainthood, in the meaning of affirming him in his state."

He said: "The people of truth spoke on the difference between the karāmah and the muʿjizah. The Imām Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī (may God have mercy on him) used to say: 'The muʿjizāt are proofs of the truthfulness of the prophets, and the evidence of prophethood is not found with other than the prophet.' And he used to say: 'The saints (awliyā') have karāmāt, among them the answering of the supplication of the year...'"

chapters.title_en: On Miracles (Muʿjizāt) and Graces (Karāmāt): Their Distinction, Conditions, and the Knowledge of Sainthood
chapters.arabic_text: فأما جنس ما هو معجزة للأنبياء فلا. وقال الإمام أبو بكر بن فورك رحمه الله تعالى المعجزات دلالات الصدق فإن ادعى صاحبها النبوة دلت على صدقه وإن أشار صاحبها إلى الولاية دلت على صدقه في حالته فتسمى كرامة ولا تسمى معجزة وإن كانت من جنس المعجزات للفرق وكان رحمه الله يقول من الفرق بين المعجزات والكرامات أن الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام مأمورن بإظهارها والولي يجب عليه سترها وإخفاؤها والنبي يدعي ويقطع القول به والولي لا يدعيها ولا يقطع بكرامته لجواز أن يكون ذلك فكرا وقال أوحد وقته في فنه القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني رضي الله تعالى عنه المعجزات تختص بالأنبياء والكرامات تظهر للأولياء ولا يكون للأولياء معجزة لأن من شرط المعجزة إقتران دعوى النبوة بها والمعجزة لم تكن معجزة لعينها وإنما كانت. معجزة لحصولها على أوصاف كثيرة فمتى اختل شرط من تلك الشرائط لا تكون معجزة واحد تلك الشرائط دعوى النبوة والولي لا يدعي النبوة فالذي يظهر لا يكون معجزة واحد تلك الشرائط دعوى النبوة والولي لا يدعي النبوة فالذي يظهر لا يكون معجزة. # قال القشيري وهذا الذي قاله هو الذي نعتمده وندين به فشرائط المعجزة كلها أو أكثرها توجد في الكرامة إلا هذا الشرط الواحد فالكرامة فعل لا محالة وهو ناقض للعادة وتحصل في زمن التكليف على عبد تخصيصا له وتفضيلا، وقد يحصل اختيارية ودعائية وقد لا تحصل وقد تكون بغير اختياره في غالب الأوقات ولم يؤمر الولي بدعاء الخلق إلى نفسه ولو أظهر شيئا من ذلك عمن يكون اهلا له لجاز. # واختلف أهل الحق في الولي هل يجوز أن يعلم أنه ولي أم لا؟ فكان الإمام أبو بكر بن فورك رحمه الله يقول لا يجوز لأنه يسلبه الخوف ويوجب له الأمن وكان الأستاذ أبو علي الدقاق رحمه الله يقول بجوازه وهو الذي نؤثره ونقول به وليس ذلك بواجب في جميع الأولياء حتى يكون لكل ولي يعلم أنه ولي واجبا ولكن يجوز أن يعلم بعضهم ذلك كما لا يجوز أن يعلم بعضهم فإذا علم بعضهم أنه ولي كانت معرفته تلك كرامة له وانفرد بها وليس كل كرامة # # لولي يجب أن تكون تلك بعينها لجميع الأولياء بل إذا لم يكن لولي كرامة ظاهرة في الدنيا لم يقدح عدمها في كونه وليا بخلاف الأنبياء فإنه يجب أن تكون لهم معجزات لأن النبي مبعوث إلى الخلق فبالناس حاجة إلى معرفة صدقه ولا يعلم إلا بالمعجزة، وحال الولي بعكس ذلك لأنه ليس بواجب على الخلق ولا على الولي العلم بأنه ولي والعشرة من الصحابة رضى الله عنهم صدقوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه في أنهم من أهل الجنة. وأما قول من قال لا يجوز ذلك لأنهم تخرجهم من الخوف فلا بأس أن لا يخافوا تغيير العاقبة والذي يجدونه في قلوبهم من الهيبة والتعظيم والاجلال للحق سبحانه وتعالى يزيد على كثير من الخوف. # قال الاستاذ القشيري واعلم انه ليس للولي مساكنة إلى الكرامة التي تظهر عيه ولا ملاحظكة وربما يكون لهم في ظهور جنسها قوة يقين وزيادة بصيرة لتحققهم أن ذلك فعل الله تعالى فيستدلون بها على صحة ما هم عليه من العقائد والله أعلم. | | | | | | | فصل # # قال القشيري رحمه الله إن قيل كيف يجوز إظهار الكرامات الزائدة في المعاني على معجزات الرسل؟ قلنا هذه الكرامة لاحقة بمعجزات نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن كل من ليس بصادق في الإسلام تمتنع عليه الكرامات فكل نبي ظهرت له كرامة على واحد من أمته فهي معدودة من جملة معجزاته إذ لو لم يكن ذلك الرسول صادقا لم تظهر على من تابعه المعجزة يعني التي هي الكرامة لهذا الواحد. # # فصل # قال القشيري هل يجوز تفضيل الولي على النبي قلنا رتبة الأولياء لا تبلغ رتبة الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام للاجماع المنعقد على ذلك. # فصل # قال الأستاذ القشيري رحمه الله هذه الكرامات قد تكون إجابة دعوة وقد تكون إظهار طعام في أوان فاقه من غير سبب ظاهر أو حصول ماء في وقت عطش أو تسهيل قطع مسافة في مدة قرية أو تخليص من عدو أو سماع خطاب من هاتف وغير ذلك من فنون الأفعال المناقضة للعادة. # قال واعلم أن كثيرا من المقدورات يعلم اليوم قطعا أنه لا تجوز أن تقطع كرامة للأولياء وبالضرورة أو شبه الضرورة يعلم ذلك فمنها حصول إنسان من غير أبوين. وقلب جماد بهيمة وأمثال هذا كثيرة.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ز-ز (j-z-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of cutting off, severing; hence "jawāz" (permissibility) as the cutting through of prohibition, and "ijāzah" as making something pass.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, "jāʾiz" denotes what is rationally possible (al-mumkin), as opposed to the impossible (mustaḥīl) and the necessary (wājib); here it frames the logical permissibility of a saint knowing his own state.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of passage through; metaphorically, the "passing" of a claim or condition across the threshold of validity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Ellipsis (al-Sharṭ wa-l-Jawāb bi-l-Ḥadhf) — In "فإن ادعى صاحبها النبوة دلت على صدقه," the protasis governs the apodosis without an explicit connector, relying on the semantic entailment of the claim to prophethood.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the genus of that which is a miracle (muʿjizah) for the prophets — no, that is not [a grace]. Imam Abū Bakr ibn Fūrak (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Miracles are proofs of truthfulness. If their possessor claims prophethood, they indicate his truthfulness; and if their possessor points to sainthood (wilāyah), they indicate his truthfulness in his state, and are then termed a grace (karāmah), not a miracle — even if they are of the genus of miracles — due to the distinction [between them]. He (may Allah have mercy on him) used to say: Among the distinctions between miracles and graces is that the prophets (upon them be prayer and peace) are commanded to manifest them, while the saint (walī) is obligated to conceal and hide them. The prophet claims [prophethood] and asserts it definitively, whereas the saint does not claim [sainthood] nor assert his grace definitively, because it is possible that [what appears] be a delusion (fikr).

The unique one of his time in his art, the Judge Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī (may Allah be well pleased with him), said: Miracles are specific to the prophets, and graces appear for the saints. The saints have no miracle, because among the conditions of a miracle is the conjunction of the claim to prophethood with it. A miracle is not a miracle in its own essence; rather, it is a miracle by virtue of its attaining numerous attributes. Whenever one condition of those conditions is impaired, it is not a miracle. One of those conditions is the claim to prophethood, and the saint does not claim prophethood; thus what appears [from him] is not a miracle.

Al-Qushayrī said: This which he stated is what we adopt and hold as our religion. All the conditions of a miracle, or most of them, are found in the grace, except this single condition. Thus the grace is an act, without doubt, which breaks the custom (nāqiḍ lil-ʿādah), and occurs in the time of religious obligation (taklīf) upon a servant, as a particularization and favor for him. It may occur voluntarily and through supplication, and it may not occur; and it may occur without his choice in most instances. The saint is not commanded to call creation to himself, and if he were to manifest something of that sort from one who is worthy of it, it would be permissible.

The people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) differed concerning the saint: is it permissible for him to know that he is a saint, or not? Imam Abū Bakr ibn Fūrak (may Allah have mercy on him) held that it is not permissible, because it strips him of fear (khawf) and necessitates for him security (amn). The master Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq (may Allah have mercy on him) held its permissibility — and this is what we prefer and affirm. It is not obligatory for all saints that every saint know he is a saint; rather, it is permissible that some of them know that, just as it is not permissible that some know it. So when some of them know that he is a saint, that knowledge of his is a grace for him, and he is singled out by it. Not every grace that is for a saint must be exactly that [same grace] for all saints. Rather, if a saint has no manifest grace in this world, the absence of it does not impair his being a saint — unlike the prophets, for miracles must exist for them, because the prophet is sent to creation, and people have need of knowing his truthfulness, which is known only through the miracle. The state of the saint is the opposite of that, because it is not obligatory upon creation, nor upon the saint, to know that he is a saint. The ten Companions (may Allah be well pleased with them) believed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that they were among the people of Paradise. As for the saying of those who said that this is not permissible because it removes them from fear — there is no harm that they not fear the change of the final outcome; and what they find in their hearts of awe (haybah), veneration, and reverence for the Truth (glorified and exalted be He) exceeds much of fear.

The master al-Qushayrī said: Know that the saint has no repose in the grace that appears upon him, nor any regard for it. Perhaps for them, in the appearance of its genus, there is a strength of certainty and an increase of insight, because of their verification that it is the act of Allah (exalted be He); thus they infer from it the soundness of what they hold of beliefs. And Allah knows best.

SECTION (Faṣl)
